articles.title_orig: US arrests California man for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China
articles.title_zh: US arrests California man for allegedly smuggling $300m worth of computer servers to China
articles.content_orig:
Greg Lui allegedly used false paperwork to smuggle export-controlled gear from US to third countries and then China
US authorities have arrested a man accused of smuggling more than $300m worth of computer servers to China , the Department of Justice announced.
Greg Lui, 38, of California , also known as “Yiu Kong Lui”, allegedly used false paperwork and shipments through third countries to smuggle the export-controlled computer servers to China, the justice department said in a statement on Thursday.
The servers contained “US-manufactured graphics processing units (GPUs) commonly used for Super Intelligence (SI)”, it added, using the Trump administration’s new name for artificial intelligence (AI).
“Protecting America’s national security means keeping our advanced super intelligence technology from being used to strengthen our adversaries’ military capabilities,” the US attorney for the central district of California , Bill Essayli, said.
“We will aggressively prosecute those who put our national security at risk for profit,” he added.
Lui operated a technology company called Earthmade Computer, which he used to buy and send items to China without the licenses required by the US Department of Commerce from 2023 to 2024, according to the statement.
The company shipped the items to countries including Malaysia and Singapore, where no such license is required, then illegally re-exported them to China.
If convicted, Lui could face a maximum of 50 years in prison.
after newsletter promotion
China, long seen as trailing the United States on cutting-edge AI, has been closing that gap fast.
The United States has long tried to slow China’s progress with export controls on the advanced chips needed for cutting-edge AI, blocking access to top-end US semiconductors such as those made by Nvidia.

articles.title_orig: The world’s tallest wind turbine just reached 1,197 feet
articles.title_zh: The world’s tallest wind turbine just reached 1,197 feet
articles.content_orig:
The world’s tallest wind turbine has reached its full height in Germany, and its developer says the extra altitude could roughly double its electricity output.
GICON ‘s pilot turbine in Schipkau, eastern Germany, stands 365 meters (1,197 feet) tall, including its blades. That makes it Germany’s second-tallest structure, behind Berlin’s TV tower. Its rotor hub sits 300 meters (984 feet) above the ground.
Winds at higher altitudes are stronger and more consistent, giving the turbine more opportunities to generate electricity. GICON says its design could produce approximately twice as much energy as a conventional turbine with the same rotor diameter.
The turbine has a rated capacity of 3.8 megawatts (MW), while future versions are planned to exceed 7 MW. That projected doubling refers to electricity generated over time, rather than a doubling of the turbine’s rated power.
GICON built the project for Germany’s Federal Agency for Disruptive Innovation, or SPRIND. Official commissioning is planned for November, with final work still to be completed.
Getting the turbine that high required a different approach to construction. Instead of relying on a crane capable of reaching the full height, GICON used a telescoping tower. A specialized lifting system raised the inner tower through the surrounding lattice structure, then secured it in its extended position.
“365 meters – this is an overwhelming moment for our entire team,” said GICON founder and CEO Jochen Großmann. “What was long a challenging idea and then an equally challenging construction project now stands as a globally unique facility in Schipkau.”
The company also wants to use that extra height to get more electricity out of existing wind farms.
GICON and SPRIND envision adding these taller turbines as a “second tier,” with their rotors operating above those of conventional turbines. Their current assessment suggests Germany’s existing wind farms could potentially accommodate up to 4,000 high-altitude turbines, adding generation without developing new wind farm areas.
That’s an estimate of what might be possible, rather than an announced construction pipeline. The Schipkau turbine is still a pilot, and its projected energy yield has yet to be demonstrated in operation.
GICON and SPRIND are now preparing to scale up the design and discussing commercialization with interested wind energy companies. Their goal is to begin series production as quickly as possible. First comes commissioning, and then they’ll see how much electricity the world’s tallest wind turbine actually delivers.

articles.title_orig: Real-World Evidence and Long-Term Data for Lybalvi and Aristada
articles.title_zh: Real-World Evidence and Long-Term Data for Lybalvi and Aristada
articles.content_orig:
Real-world data show Lybalvi cuts acute care visits in schizophrenia or bipolar I with AUD, while long-acting aripiprazole offers flexible dosing and stable symptom control.
Retrospective claims analysis data showed significant reductions in hospital and emergency department visits after initiation of Lybalvi (olanzapine/samidorphan) among patients with schizophrenia or bipolar I disorder and comorbid alcohol use disorder (AUD), according to Hemangi Panchmatia, MS. Acute care events were measured in 4 categories: all-cause, mental health–related, disease-related, and AUD-related. "We saw a significant reduction across all of these 4 categories in our schizophrenia patients as well as bipolar I disorder patients who have a comorbid alcohol use disorder," Panchmatia said.
Samidorphan, an opioid antagonist with strong binding at the mu receptor, was combined with olanzapine to attenuate weight gain and metabolic dysfunction. Peripheral effects included glucose metabolism and fat accumulation, whereas central effects on the brain's reward system may have supported satiety and reduced cravings.  Antecedent studies fed into a long-term open-label extension lasting up to 4 years or beyond for many patients, and mitigation of weight gain and metabolic dysfunction was associated with better adherence and longer persistence. 1 Many patients had no significant weight gain, and metabolic parameters remained stable over a long period. Findings extended across schizophrenia and bipolar I disorder and across patients early in illness and those more typical of clinical trials. "It's important to provide your patients with an efficacious treatment that they can adhere to, that they can tolerate, and that they will stay on for long periods of time," McGrory said.
A separate clinician-focused poster summarized the development program for aripiprazole lauroxil, a long-acting injectable prodrug formulated to reduce absorption. This design allowed extended release with consistent, predictable plasma concentrations and without pronounced peak and trough effects, maintaining patients at levels relevant to their symptoms. Dosing once monthly, every 6 weeks, or every 2 months allowed clinicians to individualize intervals. Significant symptom reductions were observed on the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale, with improvement on the Clinical Global Impression–Severity scale. 2 The adverse event profile mirrored that of oral aripiprazole over an extended period, including low sedation and lower levels of metabolic dysfunction and weight gain.
Dr McGrory is medical strategy lead for psychiatry and senior medical director & product lead at Alkermes.
Ms Panchmatia is senior director and head of psychiatry HEOR at Alkermes.
1. Jain R, Penn A, Carbray J, et al. Acute care events following initiation of olanzapine/samidorphan among patients with schizophrenia or bipolar 1 disorder and comorbid alcohol use disorder. Poster presented at: Psych Congress 2026 Annual Meeting; September 15-19; New Orleans, LA. Accessed September 18, 2026.
2. Kempf B, Carbray J, Barbee R, et al. Use of an aripiprazole lauroxil injection administered once every month, 6 weeks, or 2 months in people with schizophrenia: a clinician focused summary of study data. Poster presented at: Psych Congress 2026 Annual Meeting; September 15-19; New Orleans, LA. Accessed September 18, 2026.

articles.title_orig: Lake of the Ozarks teen heads to China for wakesurfing competition
articles.title_zh: Lake of the Ozarks teen heads to China for wakesurfing competition
articles.content_orig:
A teenager from the Lake of the Ozarks will travel to China this month to compete in the 2026 IWWF World Wakesurf Championships.
Victoria Moroski, 17, is a three-time national champion and four-time Masters World champion in the WWA Wakeseries. She began wakesurfing at age 12 after a friend introduced her to the sport.
“I like to wakesurf a lot,” Moroski said. “I just like being outside and doing a lot of activities.”
Moroski said she fell in love with the sport after breaking her ankle and watching friends surf while she recovered.
“I think I fell in love with it when I broke my ankle and I had to watch everyone on the boat surf and I couldn’t do it for six months,” Moroski said.
“I was like, ‘Dang, I really want to do this.’ I think that’s when I really wanted to do it more.”
She began competing in tournaments three years ago.
“I thought it’d be really fun to compete,” Moroski said. “I like competing and trying to win trophies.”
But the trophies aren't the main reason she competes. Moroski said the real reward is the sense of accomplishment she gets from something she spends hours training for.
At 16, Moroski was selected as the best athlete in her division and joined Team USA Wakesurf.
Team USA will travel to Hangzhou, China, for the 2026 IWWF World Wakesurf Championships, scheduled for Oct. 9-17.
Moroski said athletes from 20 countries are expected to compete. It will be her first international competition.
“I’m super excited,” Moroski said. “I can’t wait to meet other surfers from different countries.”
To prepare for competitions, Moroski said she builds a routine around tricks she is confident performing and practices them repeatedly.
“I practice them over and over for hours until I get them,” Moroski said. “I’ll read my Bible, pray about it, and just stay really calm and try to do the best I know how to do.”
Her favorite trick is a 3-shuv, an aerial maneuver in which the rider pops the board out of the water and spins it 360 degrees beneath their feet before landing back on the board.
Moroski said her coaches, Whitley Stewart Roberts and Sean Silveria, and parents have been the most influential people in her wakesurfing career.
“Whitley’s the best female surfer in the world, and Sean was one of the best pro men surfers in the world,” Moroski said. “They are my coaches and teach me all my new stuff.”
Roberts is a four-time world champion, while Silveria is a one-time world champion wakesurfer and six-time world champion flowrider.
Silveria has trained several athletes, including Jett Lambert, who is described as one of the top wakesurfers in the world.
Moroski said training can be challenging, especially on days when things don’t go as planned on the water.
“Some days you have bad training days, and it makes you super frustrated,” Moroski said. “You just have to push through it.”
Moroski said wakesurfing is “really fun” and that she is excited to compete in China.
“I just can’t wait to meet everyone and make a lot of new friends there,” Moroski said.

Al-Dabbagh and Al-Hamlawi shine
Palestine thrashed China 5-0 in Friday's friendly at the Chongqing Longxing Stadium, bringing the "Fida'i" training camp in China to a close.
Osaid Al-Hamlawi opened the scoring in the 16th minute, firing home with his right foot from inside the box after Oday Dabbagh teed him up, the goal awarded following a VAR review. Six minutes later he struck again, converting Zaid Qunbar's pass to make it two, VAR confirming that one as well.

Officially: Messi returns to Spanish football
Dabbagh then got in on the act. Five minutes into first-half stoppage time, he lashed a left-footed effort into the net from inside the area after Omeed Mahajna released him, sending Palestine in three goals to the good at the break.
China threw on five substitutes at half-time, but the changes did nothing to stem the tide. Dabbagh grabbed his second and Palestine's fourth in the 54th minute, drilling a right-footed finish from the right of the box.
The hosts went close to pulling one back twice, both times from direct free-kicks that cannoned off the right post. Wang Shangyuan rattled the woodwork in the 68th minute, Liu Yang in the 79th.
Ahmed Al-Qaq completed the rout in the third minute of stoppage time, striking right-footed from the centre of the area. He had replaced Dabbagh in the 82nd minute.
Khaled Al-Nabris went into the book for Palestine in the 50th minute, with China's Gao Chunyu booked in the 68th for a violent challenge.
During the same camp, Palestine had beaten Tajikistan 4-2, a game in which Osaid Al-Hamlawi scored twice.

articles.title_orig: Uzbekistan dominates chess Olympiad while England’s Sivanandan, 11, sets new world age record
articles.title_zh: Uzbekistan dominates chess Olympiad while England’s Sivanandan, 11, sets new world age record
articles.content_orig:
Host nation won having led almost from start to finish, while young English player reached a stunning landmark
Uzbekistan, the host nation, won the open gold medals at the 2026 Olympiad, the biennial chess international team tournament, at Samarkand last week in the style of the legendary Soviet grandmasters of long ago. India, the defending champions, were second, Germany a surprise third, and the top-seeded United States fourth.
The hosts led almost from start to finish, with world No 5 Nodirbek Abdusattorov and the world title challenger Javokhir Sindarov their top-board powerhouses. The team recovered swiftly from a single defeat by Germany, and were particularly impressive in crushing Armenia by 3.5-0.5 in the penultimate round. The Uzbekistan government rewarded each of the five players with $200,000 (£178,000), a house and a Volkswagen, plus $50,000 for the coach Rustam Kasimdzhanov.
India performed in line with their seeding. Putting the world champion, Gukesh Dommaraju, on board four boosted his results but also underlined that Sindarov is the favourite for the coming world championship match. Gukesh was exposed in the final rounds when he was outplayed against both Germany, although he won that game fortuitously, and Hungary.
The final leading scores were: Uzbekistan 20/22 match points; India and Germany 18 ; USA, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Hungary 17 ; China, France, Spain, Ukraine and England 16 (206 teams competed).
England’s creditable 12th place, one below their seeding, would have been higher still if a third player had performed at the level of the nine-time British champion Michael Adams, 54, and the Spectator chess columnist Luke McShane, 42, who were both in contention for individual medals right up to the final round. England’s women were 15th against their seeding of 20th, and the combined performance was the best since at least 2018, and probably since 1990.
Russia/USSR, which monopolised Olympiad golds in the second half of the 20th century, have been banned from the last three competitions due to the invasion of Ukraine. If allowed to take part, a team of Ian Nepomniachtchi, Andrey Esipenko, Daniil Dubov, Vladislav Artemiev and Alexander Grischuk would have been contenders.
The potential of Turkey’s Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus stands out. The 15-year-old won the individual silver medal unbeaten and has advanced to No 17 in the live ratings, a similar level to Bobby Fischer at that age and well ahead of current world No 1 Carlsen when he was 15. Here he defeats a rival prodigy , Argentina’s Faustino Oro.
China won the women’s Olympiad ahead of Kazakhstan, India and the US, and did so with its B team. World champion Ju Wenjun, world No 1 Hou Yifan, former title challenger Tan Zhongyi and world No 3 Lei Tingjie all stayed at home, but their substitutes, led by world No 4 Zhu Jiner and 16-year-old Lu Miaoyi, proved highly effective.
For the future, the US is potentially a powerhouse in women’s chess. Its duo of Carissa Yip, 23, and Alice Lee, 16, are both targeting the open GM title and its $100,000 bonus offered by Dr Jeanne Cairns Sinquefield, while new candidates are emerging in Rachael Li, Rose Atwell and Zoey Tang who are all teenagers with 2300+ ratings.
Bodhana Sivanandan broke the world age record for the youngest ever woman grandmaster (WGM). Her 8/11 total, playing all games with no rest days, included six wins, draws against Ukraine’s reigning European champion Anastasiia Hnatyshyn and Georgia’s former World Blitz champion Nana Dzagnidze, both of them current world top 20 players, and a solitary loss to Deysi Cori of Peru due to a time-pressure blunder in a drawn ending.
The 11-year-old Harrow schoolgirl’s record as the youngest ever WGM broke Hou’s 2006 mark by several months, and she also recorded her second norm (of three needed) for the international master (IM) title at open level. For IM, she also needs a 2400 rating against her current 2382, which includes the Olympiad.
Her last-round Olympiad game was a model of what has become her trademark style of a Magnus Carlsen grind.
If she secures her final norm and becomes an IM before her 12th birthday, she will break the all-time female No 1 Judit Polgar’s world age record and also become one of the 10 youngest ever IMs. She is already No 2 among all players born in 2015, behind only Russia’s IM Roman Shogdzhiev, who has been groomed for several years as a potential heir to Anatoly Karpov.
after newsletter promotion
The Guardian’s Matthew Weaver interviewed Sivanandan after her return home. At the end of the Olympiad the youngster talked with Lichess.org’s Theo Wait , while chess.com also covered her achievements in detail .
The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport’s new £250,000 a year Supporting Elite Chess Fund document contains no specific provision for rewarding world-record breakers. Maybe it should, as Sivanandan’s IM title and new record could follow as soon as the London Classic, which begins in November.
Sivanandan has just started at secondary school, and that could slow her progress on the chessboard. The advance from IM to GM is difficult, and many talents eventually plateau, which should temper extrapolations of a rise comparable to Polgar and Hou.
Meanwhile Timur Turlov, 38, a Russian-born entrepreneur from Kazakhstan whose company Freedom Holding has a multibillion dollar valuation on the Nasdaq index, was elected as the new president of the world chess body Fide last Saturday.
The previous Fide President, Russia’s Arkady Dvorkovich, had planned to run for a third term but was forced to withdraw due to EU sanctions on his assets and travel visas.
Turlov received 96 votes against 76 for the German businessman Wadim Rosenstein and a surprisingly low 20 for the ticket of Jan Henric Buettner of Freestyle Chess and the ECF’s international director Malcolm Pein. In the run-off ballot they switched to Turlov, who defeated Rosenstein 110-85.
Turlov is young, committed and with proven business skills. However, there could be an immediate problem since Rosenstein has appealed to the court of arbitration for sport over the new president’s eligibility.

articles.title_orig: As Prospects Dim, G.O.P. Pulls Money Out of North Carolina Senate Race
articles.title_zh: As Prospects Dim, G.O.P. Pulls Money Out of North Carolina Senate Race
articles.content_orig:
A Republican super PAC is shifting strategy.
Senate Republicansâ top super PAC is making a tactical change, pausing its ad campaign in North Carolinaâs Senate race and launching a new one in Kansas.
Senate Leadership Fund is plowing seven figures into Kansas to help incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall against Democrat Adam Hamilton. After spending more than $30 million in North Carolinaâs Senate race, the super PAC is putting further spending there on hold. A Trump-aligned group also has no further spending on the books past this week either, according to  Ad Impact.
âSLFâs job is to maintain the majority and this move reflects the most effective and efficient use of resources to do exactly that,â said a person familiar with the plans. The group also recently boosted its spending in Senate races in Ohio and Iowa.
The move to shore up Marshall and put North Carolina on the back burner reflects a shifting Senate battleground map â and Republican Michael Whatleyâs struggles in North Carolina against former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper. Another GOP group cut millions in North Carolina ad reservations last week and some Republicans have been urging their allies to concentrate on other Senate races.
In Kansas, Hamilton is running surprisingly close to Marshall, who is seeking a second term in a state where a Democrat hasnât won a Senate race in nearly a century.
The new SLF ad hits Hamilton as a âtwo-face extremistâ and is aimed at eroding his centrist credibility with voters, dinging him on his immigration record and linking him to Democrats like Kamala Harris and Hillary Clinton and calling him âtoo-extreme for Kansas.â
Senate Republicans currently hold 53 seats, including North Carolina and Kansas, and can afford to lose up to three seats to keep the majority.

articles.title_orig: Blacksburg teen to represent Team USA at Mountain Bike World Cup
articles.title_zh: Blacksburg teen to represent Team USA at Mountain Bike World Cup
articles.content_orig:
ROANOKE, Va. (WSET) — Lucinda Cherbaka, 17, of Blacksburg, will represent Team USA at the 2026 UCI Mountain Bike World Series in Lake Placid this weekend, according to Roanoke Star Cycling.
The event draws athletes from around the world to compete in mountain bike events including cross-country and downhill.
Roanoke Star Cycling said the opportunity for Lucinda represents a major milestone in a cycling journey that began with racing cross-country mountain bikes with the New River Valley Cycling Alliance and developed into a passion for downhill. She joined the Roanoke Star Cycling Gravity Team in 2025 and has since developed as a competitive athlete through the support of her family, coaches, teammates and the broader RSC Gravity community.
“Representing Team USA is an incredible honor,” said Lucinda. “I’m excited to race at Lake Placid, learn from the experience and carry the support of my family, coaches, teammates and RSC Gravity with me.”
Since joining RSC Gravity, Lucinda has achieved a number of impressive finishes in the Pro-Women category through the Downhill Southeast Series against older and more experienced competitors:
Roanoke Star Cycling is a youth mountain biking nonprofit dedicated to helping young riders develop skills, confidence, fitness and a lifelong connection to cycling. The organization provides athletes with coaching, community and opportunities to participate in mountain biking at a variety of levels.

articles.title_orig: Spain's government dealt blow after parliament rejects housing measures. Early election speculated
articles.title_zh: Spain's government dealt blow after parliament rejects housing measures. Early election speculated
articles.content_orig:
Spain's Congress has rejected a series of measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis, in a defeat for the government of Pedro Sánchez that increases pressure on him to call a snap election.
Lawmakers voted on two decree-laws presented by the government in response to nationwide protests that have followed the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, Maricarmen Abascal, from her home.
The decrees, which introduced a series of initiatives aimed at protecting tenants in the rental market, required parliamentary approval in order to remain in place.
MPs rejected the first decree by 178 votes to 172 and voted against the second by 184 to 166.
Hundreds of demonstrators had gathered outside Congress as the debate took place and there were angry scenes.
Protesters chanted "shame on you" and "your profits, our misery", after the results were announced.
The government's defeat underlines the fact that Sánchez, a Socialist, does not command a congressional majority and it has heightened speculation that he might call an early general election, which was not due until next summer.
Sources told Spanish media that the government would spend the weekend deciding its next step, and whether to dissolve parliament.
Sánchez's beleaguered government had already been mired in a series of scandals and judicial cases affecting his Socialist Party and close allies.
Abascal was evicted after she was unable to pay a sharp rent increase introduced by Urbagestión, the company that owned her flat in central Madrid.
Hundreds of protesters gathered to oppose the eviction last week and the case triggered a broader movement across the country demanding affordable rentals, which have soared in recent years.
The social backlash has seen Urbagestión negotiate the return of Abascal to her flat on a low rent. However, protests have continued, with people occupying squares in Madrid and other cities, pitching tents in squares and with a series of marches scheduled for this weekend.
The Sindicato de Inquilinas (Tenants' Union) activist association which has been co-ordinating protests, announced during the congressional debate that it was abandoning the tent protest in central Madrid. It said it wanted to "take the struggle to all the neighbourhoods, residential blocks and homes of Madrid, wherever there are rental increases, expulsions and abuses each day, and turn the energy of the last few days into a permanent organisation".
Protesters are also calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.
The left-wing coalition government responded to the social anger by hurriedly drawing up the two decree-laws in an effort to defuse the protests.
The first decree included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by what the government calls "vulture funds".
The second decree was more controversial, because it included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Sindicato de Inquilinas .
The conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.
However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.
Friday's debate was fierce and at times angry, as supporters and opponents of the decrees clashed in Congress.
"I don't ask you, I beg you to be brave and consistent," Sánchez said, moments before the two votes took place. "Because they are not just ambitious measures, they are necessary".
He appealed to lawmakers "to put order and humanity into [the housing] market, because if we don't, it will bring down our society".
Social Affairs minister Pablo Bustinduy, of the Sumar alliance, the junior partner in the governing coalition, presented the debate in dramatic terms.
"Today is about defending an international oligarchy which is extracting the rent from salaries earned with the effort of working classes of this country in order to share it out with dividends and they don't even pay taxes in Spain," he said.
"Voting against these decrees today means defending the interests of this oligarchy and turning your back on your own people."
However, Miriam Nogueras, of JxCat, said the decrees had been hastily drawn up and lacked rigour.
She said the decrees "will allow [vulture] funds to keep buying, keep speculating and evictions to keep happening… these two decrees would provoke the opposite effect of what they aim to achieve."
The political right has argued that the government's attempts to intervene will frighten homeowners, causing them not to put their properties on the rental market and pushing prices up further.
Juan Bravo of the PP said "housing doesn't get cheaper with decrees, it gets cheaper with more homes".

articles.title_orig: Antino Backdoor Uses Outlook and OneDrive for C2 in China-Nexus Espionage Campaign
articles.title_zh: Antino Backdoor Uses Outlook and OneDrive for C2 in China-Nexus Espionage Campaign
articles.content_orig:
Government and policy organizations across Asia have become the target of a new campaign orchestrated by a China-nexus threat actor.
The activity, which has targeted government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, the Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, and Myanmar, involves the deployment of a previously undocumented backdoor codenamed Antino. Cisco Talos is tracking the cluster under the moniker UAT-11587 .
The threat actor was first detected in September 2025 in connection with a spear-phishing campaign directed against Taiwan's academic, think tank, and civil society policy community. Since then, attacks linked to the intrusion set have expanded to target 16 entities across eight Asian countries.
"Antino is a Rust-compiled Windows backdoor that supports host reconnaissance, shell and PowerShell execution, file transfer, in-memory shellcode loading and persistence," security researcher Ashley Shen said . "Its native command-and-control channel operates exclusively through Microsoft 365, using Microsoft Graph to interact with Outlook and OneDrive."
UAT-11587 is assessed to share some level of overlap with Jewelbug, which, in turn, exhibits tactical similarities with China-aligned clusters known as CL-STA-0049, Earth Alux, Ink Dragon, and REF7707. A report published by Broadcom-owned Symantec and Carbon Black in August 2026 characterized Jewelbug as a China-based hackers-for-hire group that carries out espionage operations and a for-profit cryptocurrency fraud business.
However, Cisco Talos said its own investigation has failed to unearth a connection between the espionage campaign and Jewelbug's financially motivated activity, prompting it to designate UAT-11587 as a separate activity set.
The challenges in establishing definitive links notwithstanding, the adversary has been classified as China-nexus with high confidence, citing the presence of zh-CN language and Simplified Chinese metadata in the lure documents and the UTC+08:00 time zone in the spear-phishing message header.
"The campaign's lure theme and targeting provide additional contextual support," Talos said. "Its lures and observed targets include Taiwanese political, legislative, civil defense, and policy research subjects, together with regional government, maritime, diplomatic, and security themes. This collection focus is consistent with China-nexus actor interests."
Two other indicators that point to a China-nexus are below -
Evidence indicates that UAT-11587 has also trained its sights on organizations in Syria around May 2026, indicating a focus beyond Asia. Attacks mounted by the threat actor have been found to spike between March and early June 2026, with a "concentrated wave" taking place on June 8 and 9, 2026, targeting dozens of systems associated with government IT infrastructure.
While the choice of spear-phishing as an initial access vector is unsurprising, the choice of the lures employed suggests the threat actor conducted extensive reconnaissance of the target organizations in order to tailor the content and maximize the chance of success.
In an attempt to lend credibility to the emails, UAT-11587 is said to have spoofed sender identities trusted by the intended recipients to bypass SPF and DMARC security checks and ensure that the messages land on the victims' inboxes.
"Another social engineering technique used for initial access in this campaign was the closely replicated reconstruction of Gmail's native attachment preview widget inside the email HTML body," Shen explained. "The actor replicated the styling of Gmail's attachment card using four inline PNG images embedded as Base64-encoded MIME parts."
"The entire attachment card was wrapped in an anchor tag pointing to an attacker-controlled [Cloudflare Pages] URL. When a Gmail user opens the email in a browser, Gmail's renderer faithfully displays the attacker-controlled HTML, producing a fake attachment widget that is visually indistinguishable from a legitimate Gmail attachment preview."
An analysis of the lures demonstrates a propensity to target audiences interested in foreign affairs, international security, and government policy, Talos added. The attack chain itself is a five-stage process that begins with a HTA or WSF stager and culminates in the deployment of Antino.
The Cloudflare URL in the phishing email leads to the download of an HTA or WSF file that's then executed to retrieve a JavaScript downloader and decryptor. The next stage triggers a .NET deserialization chain to load "TestAssembly.dll," a .NET downloader and launcher that's responsible for three actions -
The implant ("slc.dll") is launched by means of DLL sideloading using a legitimate Microsoft-signed binary ("GatherOsState.exe"). Once launched, the Rust-compiled malware communicates with Microsoft 365 applications and uses Outlook and OneDrive objects as dead drops, instead of depending on a conspicuous dedicated command-and-control (C2) server.
Antino is no different from other backdoors of its kind in that it supports host reconnaissance, command execution, and persistence. It can also list running processes, enumerate directories, run PowerShell scripts, shellcode, operator-supplied programs, and commands using "cmd.exe"
For C2, it uses Outlook for command exchange and OneDrive for heartbeat and file transfer. Specifically, it fetches commands from the threat actor's Outlook mailbox folder every 10 seconds by looking for messages with the subject prefix "command_req_[session_id]."
"The Antino backdoor abuses the Windows Scripted Diagnostics framework to execute attacker-controlled PowerShell through legitimate Windows components," Talos said. "This can complicate behavioral attribution to the original implant, although it does not eliminate observable PowerShell, file-creation, or Registry telemetry."
AI agents are already operating inside enterprises with growing access to sensitive systems and data—while security teams still lack the visibility, controls, and governance to keep that access in check.
Attackers are using AI to accelerate reconnaissance, compromise identities and escalate access. See how security teams can fight back with runtime identity controls.

articles.content_orig:
LAS VEGAS (October 2026) – Experts in convenient and beautiful weddings of all sizes from the Wedding Capital of the World™ share the most popular wedding date predictions for 2027. Conducting more destination weddings than any other place on the planet, the Office of the County Clerk has decades of data to help it predict next year’s special dates. Highly desired dates for nuptials in Las Vegas include unique numerical patterns—often called “magic dates”— as well as notable holidays and other trendy events.
A complete list of 2027’s top wedding dates most likely to draw thousands of couples to the destination include:
● New Year’s Day, Friday, Jan. 1
● 1/27/27 (Magic date), Wednesday, Jan. 27
● 2/2/27 (Magic date), Tuesday, Feb. 2
● 2/7/27 (Magic date), Sunday, Feb. 7
● Valentine’s Day, Sunday, Feb. 14
● 2/27/27 (Magic date), Saturday, Feb. 27
● 3/27/27 (Magic date), Saturday, March 27
● April Fool’s Day, Thursday, April 1
● 4/20/25 Pot Day, Tuesday, April 20
● 4/27/27 (Magic date), Tuesday, April 27
● May The Fourth/“Star Wars” Day, Tuesday, May 4
● 5/5/27 (Cinco de Mayo), Wednesday, May 5
● 5/27/27 (Magic date), Thursday, May 27
● 6/27/27 (Magic date), Sunday, June 27
● 7/2/27 (Magic date and palindrome), Friday, July 2
● Independence Day, Sunday, July 4
● 7/7/27 (Magic date), Wednesday, July 7
● 7/20/2027 (Magic date and palindrome), Tuesday, July 20
● 7/27/27 (Magic date and palindrome), Tuesday, July 27
● National Couple’s Day, Wednesday, Aug. 18
● 8/27/27 (Magic date), Saturday, Aug. 28
● 9/27/27 (Magic date), Monday, Sept. 27
● 10/27/27 (Magic date), Wednesday, Oct. 27
● Halloween, Sunday, Oct. 31.
● Las Vegas Marries the Military/Veterans Day, Tuesday, Nov. 9
● 11/11/27 (Magic date), Thursday, Nov. 11
● 11/27/27 (Magic date), Saturday, Nov. 27
● Christmas Day, (Saturday, Dec. 25)
● 12/27/27 (Magic date), Monday, Dec. 27
● New Year’s Eve, Friday, Dec. 31
“We have seen firsthand how ‘magic dates’ capture the attention of couples from around the world,” said Lynn Marie Goya, Clark County Clerk. “With so many fun numerical patterns on the 2027 calendar, we expect partners planning their big day will once again make Las Vegas the place to turn a memorable date into an unforgettable celebration.”
Historically, the most popular wedding date in Las Vegas occurred on 7/7/2007. It became known as the “Lucky 7s” day when 4,492 couples were married. The second most popular wedding date in Las Vegas history occurred on 11/11/2011 when 3,125 couples were married. In 2022, 2/22/22 also became the sixth most popular wedding date in the city’s history with 2,331 weddings.
With an average of 3-4% of visitors traveling to Las Vegas for weddings, wedding tourism in Clark County generates approximately $3 billion in economic output annually. Las Vegas’ wedding industry also generates 18,000 direct jobs and supports hundreds of small businesses.
For more information about the Wedding Capital of the World™ or the Office of the Clark County Clerk, Nevada, visit weddings.vegas .
ABOUT THE OFFICE OF THE CLARK COUNTY CLERK
The Honorable Lynn Marie Goya runs the Office of the Clark County Clerk that has won numerous local, national and international accolades that highlight Goya’s commitment to good government, including garnering awards for innovation, saving tax dollars, environmental stewardship, constituent outreach, efficiency and the transformation of the “Vegas wedding” brand from “The Hangover” to one of fun, stress-free excitement. The office is also responsible for numerous other government services, including passport acceptance, lobbyist registration, fictitious firm name certificates and maintaining the permanent records for the Clark County Commission Boards. For more information on the Office of the Clark County Clerk, visit clarkcountynv.gov .
ABOUT THE WEDDING CAPITAL OF THE WORLD ™
For over a century, a “Vegas wedding” has captured public imagination as the ultimate stress-free, fun, glamorous and romantic wedding, whether it is a spur-of-the-moment occasion or an elaborately planned extravaganza for 600 guests. Offering weddings for every budget—including elopements at iconic Las Vegas chapels, elaborate nuptial celebrations at the Strip’s most elegant resorts and everything in between—the destination delivers dream weddings of every description for every budget. The Clark County Marriage License Bureau, overseen by the Honorable Lynn Marie Goya, issued more than 70,000 marriage licenses in 2025, adding to its reputation as a world-recognized premier wedding destination. Marriages are tracked in the United States by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that compiles an annual Marriage Rate by State, calculating the number of marriages per thousand population. With more than 5 million weddings and counting, Nevada’s marriage rate is 24.6 as opposed to the national marriage rate of 6.1 per thousand; Hawaii’s rate is 12.5 per thousand and Florida’s 7.0 per thousand. Internationally, marriage rates for countries typically range from 5 to 10 per thousand population. But it isn’t just the numbers. Once known as the “Niagara Falls of the West” with the famous Las Vegas Strip called “Honeymoon Highway,” on Sept. 23, 1953, the London Daily Herald first called Las Vegas the “Wedding Capital of the World.” For more information about the Wedding Capital of the World™ or the Office of the Clark County Clerk, Nevada, visit weddings.vegas .

articles.title_orig: Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner, Ken Urker, dies at 34
articles.title_zh: Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner, Ken Urker, dies at 34
articles.content_orig:
Ken Urker, Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s partner and father of her child, died Thursday on his 34th birthday, according to multiple media reports.
Video above: Gypsy Rose Blanchard released from prison in 2023
His cause of death is not known at this time.
Urker was found unresponsive at his Louisiana home on Thursday by a family member, according to People . Officers were called to the home at around 6:15 p.m., and Urker was found "dead upon arrival," the Lafourche Parish Sheriff’s Office confirmed to People.
His death is under investigation.
"I’m in disbelief. I can’t think," Blanchard told People magazine Friday. "I've screamed until my throat burns."
"There are no words that can express the depth of this loss," she added. "I ask for privacy and compassion for our daughter, our families, and everyone grieving Ken during this incredibly painful time."
Blanchard became infamous due to her role in the killing of her abusive mother. She was released from prison in December 2023 after serving more than seven years of a 10-year prison sentence. Blanchard was the victim of Munchausen syndrome by proxy, in which a caregiver fakes their child’s illness or induces symptoms to make their child ill.
Blanchard met Urker while she was in prison. Urker had written a "supportive letter, not on any kind of romantic level" to Blanchard, and included his phone number, after watching "Mommy Dead and Dearest," which was released in 2017, Blanchard said on the "We Need to Talk" podcast in June.
She added that she gave Urker a call and "within five minutes of talking on the phone, I felt like we had known each other our whole lives." After two years of dating, the couple got engaged while she was in prison, but Urker split up with her months later, she said.
Blanchard went on to marry Louisiana teacher Ryan Anderson in a prison wedding ceremony in July 2022, but they parted ways in 2023, and she rekindled her romance with Urker.
Urker and Blanchard share a daughter together named Aurora Raina Urker. The couple got engaged in October 2018 and then broke up. They reunited in April 2024, shortly after Blanchard's divorce from Ryan Anderson, and their daughter was born Dec. 28, 2024.
CNN contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.title_zh: BioMarin Announces Five-Year Phase 3 Data for POMBILITI® + OPFOLDA® at World Muscle Society Annual Congress
articles.content_orig:
Long-term data reinforce durable efficacy and safety of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in late-onset Pompe disease
BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc . (Nasdaq: BMRN ) today announced new data evaluating the efficacy and safety of POMBILITI® (cipaglucosidase alfa-atga) + OPFOLDA® (miglustat) in late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) were presented at the 31st Annual Congress of the World Muscle Society (WMS), in Hiroshima, Japan.
These results from the PROPEL open-label extension (OLE) study of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA, which were shared in a late-breaking presentation, demonstrated durable motor function outcomes and relative stabilization of pulmonary function over long-term follow-up. The analysis included data from 82 individuals who received POMBILITI + OPFOLDA continuously from baseline observed in the initial PROPEL study (PROPEL baseline) to year five. For the enzyme replacement therapy (ERT)-experienced cohort, the mean duration of prior ERT at baseline was 7.6 years. These data represent long-term benefits for people with LOPD followed in the study, including both ERT-experienced and ERT-naïve cohorts.
"These five-year results demonstrate that POMBILITI and OPFOLDA can provide durable, long-term benefits for people living with late-onset Pompe disease, including those who had been on enzyme replacement therapy for years before enrolling in the study," said Greg Friberg, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Research & Development Officer at BioMarin. "Sustaining motor function and limiting pulmonary decline for up to five years in a progressive disease like LOPD is clinically meaningful, and we remain committed to continuing to share long-term evidence to inform the care of people with this rare genetic condition."
Table 1. Efficacy Measures With POMBILITI + OPFOLDA From PROPEL Baseline (BL) for up to Five Years
Mean (standard deviation, SD) change from baseline in % predicted six-minute walk distance (pp6MWD)
Mean (SD) change from baseline in % predicted forced vital capacity (ppFVC)
No new safety signals were identified. 51.2% of participants (n=42) experienced treatment-related adverse events, the majority of which were manageable. Five individuals discontinued treatment for safety reasons, including two due to serious treatment-related adverse events (chills and hypoxia [n=1], anaphylactoid reaction [n=1]).
Phase 1/2 Data Show Positive Dystrophin Expression and Favorable Tolerability With Nivudirsen (BMN 351)
Additional presentations at WMS included data evaluating nivudirsen (BMN 351), an investigational antisense oligonucleotide for ambulatory boys ages 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 51 skipping. Included in these presentations was an update from the ongoing Phase 1/2 351-201 study, which was previously shared at the 19th International Congress on Neuromuscular Diseases in July. Results from 351-201 showed treatment with nivudirsen was generally well tolerated and led to consistently positive outcomes across multiple measures of therapeutic benefit, including expression of near full-length dystrophin.
Below are key presentations at WMS, with all times listed in Japan Standard Time:
Phase 1/2 Results of BMN 351, an Antisense Oligonucleotide for Exon 51 Skip-Amenable Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Poster Presentation #2.66P Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Comprehensive Panel of Pharmacokinetic, Pharmacodynamic and Biomarker Measures Drives Clinical Development of BMN 351 for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy E-Poster Presentation #2.43eP Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Muscle Composition and Muscle Injury Biomarkers Improve With BMN 351 Treatment E-Poster Presentation #2.59eP Wednesday, Sept. 30, 5:15 – 6:15 p.m.
Long-Term (Five-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline E-Poster Presentation #3.081LBeP Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Long-Term (Four-Year) Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease Treated From PROPEL Baseline Poster Presentation #3.56P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
Baseline Disease Burden and Real-World Monitoring Practices: Global Insights From the followME Pompe Journey Registry Poster Presentation #3.57P Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
ATB200-03/07 Danish Subpopulation: Four-Year Efficacy and Safety of Cipaglucosidase Alfa Plus Miglustat in Adults With Late-Onset Pompe Disease E-Poster Presentation #3.35eP Friday, Oct. 2, 2:15 – 3:15 p.m.
About the PROPEL Open-Label Extension Study
The Phase 3 open-label extension (OLE) study (ATB200-07; NCT04138277 ) is a multicenter, international study designed to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of POMBILITI + OPFOLDA in adults with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) who completed the Phase 3 PROPEL study (ATB200-03; NCT03729362 ). Of the 118 people treated in the OLE, 82 continued POMBILITI + OPFOLDA treatment from PROPEL (62 ERT-experienced prior to PROPEL; 20 ERT-naïve) and 37 switched from the comparator arm to POMBILITI + OPFOLDA (29 ERT-experienced; eight ERT-naïve).
The study evaluates long-term changes from PROPEL baseline in six-minute walk distance (6MWD, the primary endpoint in PROPEL), forced vital capacity (FVC), creatine kinase (CK) and hexose tetrasaccharide (Hex4) levels, and patient-reported outcomes, as well as long-term safety.
The 351-201 trial ( NCT06280209 ) is a Phase 1/2 multicenter open-label dose-escalation study evaluating BMN 351 for the treatment of boys aged 4 to 10 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy with a specific genetic change amenable to exon 51 skipping. The primary endpoints examine the safety and tolerability of BMN 351, the secondary endpoints assess plasma, urine and muscle pharmacokinetics, and key exploratory endpoints include exon-skipping efficiency, dystrophin expression, immunogenicity and functional assessments.
The study is being conducted in three cohorts, with Cohort 1 being divided into Cohort 1A and Cohort 1B. In Cohort 1A, three boys received increasing doses once every two weeks with a visit to assess safety measures collected the week after dosing prior to escalating doses of BMN 351. In part two, the participants in Cohort 1A transitioned to once-weekly dosing. The participants in Cohort 1B, 2 and 3 will receive low (6 mg/kg), medium (9 mg/kg) and high (12 mg/kg) doses of BMN 351 and continue once-weekly dosing at that same dose.
For more information, please visit clinicaltrials.biomarin.com .
About Late-Onset Pompe Disease
Late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) is an inherited lysosomal disorder caused by deficiency of the enzyme acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA). Reduced or absent levels of GAA lead to accumulation of glycogen in cells, which is believed to result in the clinical manifestations of Pompe disease. LOPD can be severe and debilitating with progressive muscle weakness throughout the body that worsens over time, particularly in skeletal muscles and muscles that control breathing.
About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe neuromuscular condition that leads to progressive muscle weakness and premature mortality. DMD is caused by genetic changes that result in the absence or dysfunction of dystrophin, an essential protein that is necessary for preserving muscle function.
As an X-linked disorder, DMD primarily affects young boys, with onset of symptoms occurring around 2 to 3 years of age. The incidence of DMD is up to 1 in 3,600 to 6,000 live male births.
Individuals with DMD experience serious functional impairments, including loss of limb strength and ambulation, and respiratory and cardiovascular impacts that require lifelong care.
POMBILITI + OPFOLDA is a two-component therapy that consists of cipaglucosidase alfa-atga, a bis-M6P-enriched rhGAA that facilitates high-affinity uptake through the M6P receptor while retaining its capacity for processing into the most active form of the enzyme, and the oral enzyme stabilizer

articles.title_orig: BU Welcomes Inaugural Class of Davis United World College Scholars
articles.title_zh: BU Welcomes Inaugural Class of Davis United World College Scholars
articles.content_orig:
BU’s inaugural group of Davis Scholars–international students from select high schools–will gather periodically throughout the year to share experiences and insights.
Boston University welcomed 37 international freshmen this fall as its first Davis United World College Scholars . Based at Vermont’s Middlebury College, Davis UWC is the largest source of financial aid for international undergraduates in the United States, awarding scholarships to graduates of 18 designated high schools across the globe. BU President Melissa Gilliam arranged BU’s admission to Davis’s participating network of 100-plus American colleges and universities.
The scholarships cover students’ full, demonstrated need for the cost of attending BU: tuition, housing, and fees. (Financial needs vary by student, but most require aid to cover the full attendance cost.) This year’s inaugural cohort represents22 nations enrolled in seven BU schools and colleges. The goal is to grow the program to 80 enrolled scholars by the end of the second year.
Each scholar has a faculty or staff mentor assigned to them for their undergraduate years, and each mentor in turn advises a small group of Davis Scholars, bringing them together once a month in addition to individual meetings. Mentors will connect students with academics and experiential learning aligned with their interests. All scholars will gather several times throughout the year for special events, including faculty dinners and a Boston cultural outing. Overseeing the implementation of the program throughout the year are Laura Johnson, senior assistant provost for undergraduate affairs, and Anne Corriveau, director of international admissions.
Before coming to BU, Gilliam’s roles at the University of Chicago included chief of family planning and contraceptive research. “I saw firsthand the incredible talent, maturity, and global awareness Davis Scholars brought to that campus,” she wrote in her Davis UWC admission request. “Similar to your program’s five pillars, global engagement is a key element of BU’s DNA and a necessary component to our University’s and our students’ ability to have a positive impact across the world. BU has a long and rich history of being a global university and for enrolling international students.”
Davis Scholarships are “an extraordinary complement to Boston University’s commitment to making a world-class education accessible to talented students from around the globe,” says Kelly Walter, BU associate vice president for enrollment and dean of admissions.
BU Today spoke with two of BU’s inaugural Davis Scholars—both enrolled at the Questrom School of Business—who shared their stories and hopes for their time at the University.
“Yasmine, you’re really outspoken,” a friend once told Gerverk, who doesn’t argue the point. At her school in the Norwegian city of Moss, whenever a teacher asked a question and waited for someone’s hand to go up, “normally, it was me. I’ll take one for the class,” Geverk says. That outspokenness so impressed peers that they admitted her to the youth municipal council, an advisory group to the city government on youth perspectives, at the record-young age of 13. She ultimately served on Norway’s arm of the European Youth Parliament.
Her personal story—daughter of a Kurdish Iranian engineer and a Norwegian teacher, growing up in an immigrant neighborhood of Moss, going aboard to attend an internationally diverse UWC high school in the Netherlands—reinforced her desire to attend BU with its international student body and to participate in the Davis UWC program.
“I’ve kind of lived between cultures,” Geverk says, “a Norwegian culture and the Kurdish, Middle Eastern culture.” She roomed at her Dutch high school with students from Ukraine, China, the Netherlands, Oman, Georgia, and Bhutan. “One of the main reasons I applied to Davis United World Colleges is because I knew I would meet people from all over the world. That’s also why I wanted to pursue studying at a school that was really priding itself on being international.”
Post-graduation, Geverk plans to pursue a career in business. While she might get involved with student government at BU, she’s also interested in such activities as Innovate@BU and Questrom’s Entrepreneurship Club .
“Most likely, not having the Davis Scholarship would mean that I would have to go back home for university, or to another Scandinavian country” where higher education is less expensive than in the US, she explains. “That wasn’t something that I wanted. I wanted to go out and explore more. So without Davis, I would not be able to do that. And I feel like I wouldn’t get this level of an education without Davis.”
Geverk is determined to take advantage of all that Boston University has to offer—both in the classroom and beyond. “You lose 100 percent of the shots you don’t take,” she says.
Silja (she’s asked that her last name not be used for privacy reasons) co-led a “Human Library”—a periodic gathering during the school year in which students shared stories, some personal (identity, family conflicts, religious or cultural upbringing), others global–at her Finnish high school . “We wanted to create an environment,” she says, “where students practiced listening not necessarily with the intent of agreeing, but with the intent of understanding.” The library’s student leaders worked with speakers before each session to help them develop and share their stories.
“On the day of the event, we decorated our school library with warm lights, pillows, and candles to give the space an intimate feel,” she says. “It made me realize how easy it is to judge another individual based on our own upbringing and the values that were shaped by our surroundings. I often found myself wondering that, if I had grown up where the person I disagree with did, surrounded by the same experiences, fears and values they had, how differently might I see the world?”
Silja is exploring how she could start a similar initiative at BU, including the use of social media to share stories to reach busy students at this vast institution. She’s also looking for existing student groups touching on her passions, which include business and international relations. “I’m still very new to BU, so I’m trying to leave room to discover things I might not have expected to be interested in.”
A double major in business and international relations, she was looking at US and European colleges before BU and the Davis scholarship beckoned: “BU ultimately offered most of what I was looking for: a large and diverse student body, a vibrant urban campus, and the opportunity to pursue my interests in both business and international relations. I think the Davis program is a wonderful way to continue the UWC experience beyond high school by bringing students to universities across the US. I love that the Davis network allows that community to extend beyond UWC itself, which makes the program especially meaningful to me.
“Coming to university in a new country can be intimidating, so there is something really comforting about knowing that there is already a wider UWC community here.”
“What distinguishes the Davis Program is that it is about much more than financial support,” says Walter. “It invests in students who have already demonstrated an extraordinary commitment to cross-cultural understanding, leadership, service, and academic excellence through the United World Colleges movement.”

articles.title_zh: Indian pilot tells PM Modi he opened flydubai cockpit door during attack
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump said Friday that "Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked diesel oil" and that "the process will begin immediately."
The announcement comes as energy prices remain elevated during the U.S. war against Iran.
The Group of Seven nations released a statement Friday saying it "convened a virtual meeting to address the deepening challenges to our energy security.
"Facing unprecedented volatility in oil markets - with surging prices threatening economic stability and the well-being of our citizens - we have agreed on decisive, coordinated measures to stabilize immediate energy supplies, shield households and businesses from price shocks, and strengthen the long-term resilience of global energy systems," the statement read.
It added that the nations will conduct "a coordinated release through the International Energy Agency of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over 4 months, including a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G7 members and partners."
An Israeli plumber who helped subdue the suspected attacker during an apparent hijacking attempt on a FlyDubai flight met with U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee on Friday.
Huckabee identified the man as Yaniv and said he came to the U.S. Embassy in Jerusalem after the incident.
"Israeli plumber who heroically subdued terrorist & grabbed the controls of plane came to @usembassyjlm & I gave him my autographed hat from @POTUS," Huckabee wrote on X. "Yaniv & Meital Hayoun inspired the world. He loves @realDonaldTrump & I'll post his message to @POTUS later. What a story!"
The meeting comes after a FlyDubai flight traveling from the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia Wednesday after the pilot allegedly was stabbed by his co-pilot in the cockpit.
President Donald Trump said Thursday that Iran would be hit "very hard" if investigators determine Tehran was behind the suspected hijacking attempt.
The United States and international partners reaffirmed Friday their commitment to countering Iran's nuclear and ballistic missile programs, one year after United Nations restrictions on Tehran returned to force.
In a joint statement released by the State Department, the U.S. and Proliferation Security Initiative partners said they would continue taking measures to prevent the supply, sale or transfer to Iran of materials, equipment and technology that could contribute to proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities or nuclear weapon delivery systems.
The countries also committed to preventing prohibited transfers involving weapons of mass destruction, their means of delivery, including UAVs, and other materials covered by the reinstated UN arms restrictions.
"We welcome all national-level efforts to implement our UNSCR obligations, as well as relevant activities that support our objective of preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, such as those linked to Operation Economic Outcast," the statement said.
The countries also called on Iran to comply with its nonproliferation obligations, cooperate fully with the International Atomic Energy Agency and address international concerns about its nuclear program.
The Treasury Department announced Friday that its Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned "a member of Hamas’s military wing, along with two France-based individuals and two affiliated entities that provide critical financing to Hamas."
“These designations expose a sophisticated, multi‑year financing architecture that moved more than $2 million to Hamas through deceptive charitable fronts and cryptocurrency channels, demonstrating the organization’s persistent ability to adapt its fundraising mechanisms to evade detection,” the department said in a statement.
It added that Saleem Abdallah Saleem al-Zaq, who was targeted in Friday's action, "is a Gaza-based battalion deputy in the Hamas military wing who oversees a financial network that has used various money services businesses and cryptocurrency wallets to transfer significant funds to the Hamas Al-Qassam Brigades.
"Faouzi Barika (Barika) and Amel Oualid (Oualid) operate from France, where they run purported charities ostensibly to raise money for humanitarian purposes to aid Gazan civilians.  In reality, they partner with al-Zaq to raise and transfer money directly to him, which al-Zaq in turn funnels to Hamas," it continued.
State Department spokesman Thomas Pigott said “this action underscores the enduring U.S. commitment to dismantling Hamas’s global support networks and denying the group the resources it needs to plan and carry out terrorism that threatens the security of Americans, our partners, and the broader Middle East.
“It reflects close coordination between the Department of State, the Department of the Treasury, and the FBI to expose how Hamas exploits humanitarian and charitable structures abroad to disguise terrorist financing as legitimate aid work," he also said.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) said Friday that a tanker has been struck while traveling through the Strait of Hormuz.
"The Master of a tanker has reported being struck by an unknown projectile, whilst conducting an outbound transit, resulting in a small fire and blackout onboard. The fire has since been extinguished and the vessel is underway," the UKMTO said.
"There are no reported casualties or environmental impact," it added.
An Iranian lawmaker claimed Friday that Tehran is in control of the Strait of Hormuz, a report said.
Mohammadreza Rezaei Kouchi, the head of the Iranian parliament’s civil affairs committee, said Iran's military has “full intelligence and operational oversight” of the key waterway, according to Iran International.
“Any vessel seeking to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, and any developments there, will be subject solely to the will of Iran’s armed forces,” he reportedly added.
President Donald Trump said Wednesday that the United States has “almost total control” of the Strait of Hormuz.
“I would say total control,” he said before adding that “everyone said, 'Well, they'll drop a mine in there and disrupt things a little bit,' but we have virtually total control of the strait.”
Fox News Digital's Emma Bussey contributed to this post.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) said in a new report issued Friday that the threat environment in the Middle East "remains elevated" for commercial shipping as "no diplomatic resolution has been achieved."
It assessed the risks as following: "Strait of Hormuz SEVERE (hostile action highly likely, continued navigation interference and potential mining activity); Gulf of Oman MODERATE (ongoing electronic interference and enforcement activity); Arabian Gulf MODERATE (navigation interference and residual kinetic risk remain present)."
In the Strait of Hormuz, “Commercial vessels continue to be targeted on the southern route, with ongoing military activity sustaining an increased risk to maritime operations,” according to UKMTO.
“Since 6 Jul 26, 31 of 48 projectile strike incidents reported to UKMTO have occurred on the southern Omani route. There is probably other projectile strikes occurring that have NOT been reported to UKMTO," it also said.
The warnings come as Reuters, citing data from S&P Global Energy, reported Friday that 19 liquefied natural gas cargoes exited the Strait of Hormuz in September, the highest monthly level since the onset of the U.S.-Iran war in February.
The Israel Defense Forces announced Friday that it has killed a Hamas sniper who was planning "to carry out terror attacks against IDF forces."
“Last night, the IDF and Shin Bet attacked in the Khan Younis area and eliminated the terrorist Thamer Hamaida, who served as a sniper in the Hamas terror organization,” the IDF said.

articles.title_orig: 'Sometimes it's more expensive than having humans': Honeywell and Ecolab get real about AI's limits in the physical world
articles.title_zh: 'Sometimes it's more expensive than having humans': Honeywell and Ecolab get real about AI's limits in the physical world
articles.content_orig:
Putting the latest AI models into buildings, factories and kitchens is much harder than putting them into a chatbot. That was the message from executives at Honeywell and Ecolab , though they were fairly positive about AI overall.
Honeywell Chief Technology Officer Suresh Venkatarayalu said at Fortune ’s AIQ Summit at the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday that the problem is accuracy. The industrial giant’s customers “really demand 99.9999%,” he said, while frontier models “could be at 85%.”
Ecolab Chief AI Officer AJ Wijesinghe described a different limit: cost. When the company put “the best model that’s out there” on high-volume work, “the tokenomics go off the roof,” he said. “Sometimes it’s more expensive than having humans.”
The water-management company then optimized its models and cut token costs by about 70% to 80%, he said. Ecolab uses both frontier and open-source models, including Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s. “Sometimes you don’t have to have the fastest car,” he said.
Neither executive described a fully autonomous future. Venkatarayalu said the move is toward “a semi-autonomous world” where operators build trust in the systems, and that “autonomy is also not about removing people.” Wijesinghe described a “human in the lead” model, saying agent technology “is not matured enough” to run at scale on its own.
Physical equipment can’t be updated like a phone. Venkatarayalu said over-the-air upgrades are coming to commercial buildings, but with an operator in the loop. Buildings and industrial sites are “mission critical and safety critical,” he said. A Tesla can be down for 1.5 hours for an update, but “you cannot afford to have a building shut down for one and a half hours.”
Moderator Emily Forlini, senior AI reporter at Fortune , noted the company recently announced a partnership with Nvidia at its investor day. Venkatarayalu said it’s fine-tuning open-source models partly because customers want sovereignty over their data and models. He said Honeywell hand-picks them and works with Nvidia’s Nemotron team, because an unsupported open-source model without guardrails would be “dangerous.”
Honeywell describes a “see, think, act, and learn” framework. It starts by cataloguing a building’s assets, including HVAC, fire control, and security and access control, and connecting them over the BACnet protocol. AI agents then learn how the systems relate and run them. Venkatarayalu also said the company is exploring how to teach AI about chemistry, such as catalyst formulation.
Ecolab uses sensors in dishwashers, pest traps and water systems to cut service visits and predict maintenance. Its executive said the company also manages water for chip production, power and cooling in AI infrastructure.
An audience member from a systems integrator asked what separates AI work that creates value from work that stalls. Wijesinghe said individual AI adds little measurable value at the enterprise level, and vertical AI within a function adds some. The most value, he said, comes from “horizontal” AI that works backward from an outcome across functions such as sales, finance and supply chain.
AI “should not be just another technology,” he said, and should be tied to a company-wide transformation. Ecolab expects $325 million in annual run-rate savings by 2027, and he said “significant” amounts are already in hand. Data foundation, process readiness and cost discipline matter equally, he said: “If one is heavier than the other, then you don’t get the value.”
Honeywell’s executive said where AI runs, at the edge, on a customer’s premises or in the cloud, depends on latency, data-transaction cost and sovereignty. Customers who got 7% energy savings from existing controls now ask whether AI can deliver 30% or 40% more, he said.
For this story, Fortune journalists used generative AI as a research tool. An editor verified the accuracy of the information before publishing.
Nick Lichtenberg is business editor and was formerly Fortune 's executive editor of global news.

articles.title_orig: U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs in September, signaling a slower labor market
articles.title_zh: U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs in September, signaling a slower labor market
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. economy created far fewer jobs than expected in September, pointing to a surprising soft spot in the labor market and broader economy.
Nonfarm payrolls rose a seasonally adjusted 29,000 for the month while the unemployment rate increased to 4.2%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday. Economists surveyed by Dow Jones had been looking for job growth of 84,000 and an unemployment rate of 4.1%.
In addition to the weakness in September, the August jobs count was revised lower to reflect a gain of 133,000 while July switched from a gain to a loss as payrolls fell by 10,000. The revisions in total showed 60,000 fewer jobs than previously reported.
Market reaction was swift to the report, with traders interpreting the soft jobs numbers as good news as they likely further cemented the Federal Reserve staying put at its October meeting.
Stock futures rose sharply after the release while Treasury yields slumped after recently rising to levels not seen since the early part of the century. Market-implied odds that the Fed will hold rates steady at its Oct. 27-28 meeting jumped to 82.8%, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
"For the Fed, this number should be the nail in the coffin for an October hike," Thomas Simons, chief U.S. economist at Jefferies, said in a note.
"The payroll data surged in August, and we had expected the momentum to continue this month, given the historically low prints on jobless claims in recent weeks," he added. "However, it now appears that the August number was nothing more than a rebound from very weak hiring in June and July."
Fed officials more closely watch the unemployment rate than the headline payrolls numbers.
The household survey, which is used to calculate the jobless level, was considerably better than the establishment survey, which is used to derive the payrolls count.
Household employment rose by 406,000 for the month, while the labor force swelled by 485,000 and the participation rate, which counts those working or actively searching for a job as a share of the total labor force, increased 0.2 percentage point to 61.8%, its highest since May.
An alternative measure of unemployment, which includes discouraged workers and those holding part-time jobs for economic reasons, edged down to 7.6%, its lowest since January 2025.
The report comes with Federal Reserve officials weighing the state of the economy and how it should affect their next interest rate move.
Following statements in recent days from central bank policymakers, markets have recalibrated expectations and now expect the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee to hold off until December for its next hike. The FOMC raised benchmark rates a quarter percentage point in September.
Policymakers largely see inflation as a larger threat to the economy than the labor market, which had shown resilience in recent months. The data has painted a picture of a low-hire, low-fire economy, with weekly jobless claims low and one indicator showing layoffs at their lowest rate in four years.
Inflation, though, has held well above the Fed's 2% target. The most recent indicator of the central bank's preferred gauge showed core inflation at a 3% annual rate.
Wages, though, continued to show signs of disinflation.
Average hourly earnings increased just 0.1% in September, putting the 12-month gain at 3%, the lowest since May 2021. Wall Street had been looking for readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, respectively. The average work week was unchanged at 34.6 hours.
"Americans are frustrated by the lack of opportunities right now," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "Wage growth fell to a new 5-year low and is being wiped out entirely by inflation. That stings heading into the holidays."
However, Long described the labor market as "stable" and said she doesn't think the Fed will be dissuaded from hiking in December.
Most of the monthly job gains came from healthcare, which added 17,000 workers. Construction was up by 11,000, and manufacturing added 9,000.
Government employment fell by 17,000, while temporary help services saw a decline of 11,000, and information services lost 10,000 amid worries over the impact artificial intelligence may have on the jobs picture. Financial activities also saw a drop of 7,000 jobs.
The weak job growth comes despite signs of strength elsewhere.
On a macro level, economic growth has been strong.
Earlier this week, the Commerce Department revised its count of both first- and second-quarter gross domestic product growth, to 2.5% and 2.2%, respectively. The Atlanta Fed is tracking third-quarter GDP at 3.7%.

articles.title_orig: Look up for Saturn this weekend
articles.title_zh: Look up for Saturn this weekend
articles.content_orig:
Saturn is at its biggest and brightest as the ringed planet reaches opposition this weekend.
Opposition happens as Earth passes between Saturn and the Sun, bringing the planet to its closest point to Earth for the year, about 784 million miles (1.26 billion km) away. This minimum distance makes Saturn appear brighter than at any other time this year.
Opposition is a great time to observe Saturn because it rises in the east around sunset, reaches its highest point around midnight, and remains visible through dawn. It will appear as a yellowish point of light in the eastern and southeastern sky.
You do not need a telescope to see Saturn, but even a small telescope can reveal the planet's rings and the brightest couple of its 293 moons. While you are spotting Saturn, look a bit higher for a large grouping of four stars astronomers call the Great Square of Pegasus. Up and to the right is the Circlet (ring) of Pisces. These are asterisms, or recognizable patterns within the more official constellations of Pegasus (the winged horse) and Pisces (the fish).
2026's view is very different from last year's when Earth crossed the plane of Saturn’s rings. Though the ring system spans about 175,000 miles, it is, on average, about 30 feet thick, so it effectively disappears when viewed edge-on. Since opposition in 2025, the rings are tilted 7.5 degrees from our perspective, bringing them back into view.
Saturn will be at opposition on Sunday morning at 8:21 a.m., but with clouds expected this weekend, the best views will be tonight, Friday, Oct. 2. The planet will remain an excellent evening target for much of the month.
Saturn’s last opposition occurred Sept. 21, 2025. Saturn reaches opposition every 378 days, or about two weeks later each year, as Earth catches up with Saturn in its orbit. We'll have similar good opportunities to view Jupiter as it reaches its own opposition on Feb. 11, 2027, followed by Mars on Feb. 19, 2027.
