articles.title_orig: California man smuggled $300 million in Nvidia chips to China, prosecutors say
articles.title_zh: California man smuggled $300 million in Nvidia chips to China, prosecutors say
articles.content_orig:
Prosecutors allege that a California man helped smuggle $300 million in Nvidia chips to China.
It is illegal to export advanced semiconductor chips into China without a license.
Prosecutors say Yiu Kong Lui conspired with foreign shipping companies to trick US manufacturers.
A California man is facing federal charges for helping smuggle over $300 million worth of Nvidia semiconductor chips into China, prosecutors said this week.
Yiu Kong Lui, 38, of San Gabriel, Cali., was arrested on Thursday and is set to be arraigned in federal court and charged with violating export controls, smuggling, and money laundering, court records show.
It is illegal to export advanced semiconductor chips into China without a license, as the US competes with the East Asian giant in the AI race.
President Donald Trump drew criticism last year for allowing Nvidia to sell its chips to China , a departure from the previous US policy under President Joe Biden, which effectively blocked all exports of advanced chips to China.
Nvidia's chips are especially sought after for use in AI data centers because they can perform multiple calculations simultaneously, and because the company's software stack is widely compatible.
In a press release, US officials said Liu put US national security at risk by smuggling the chips.
"Controlling the export of advanced SI technology is critical to safeguarding our national security and defending the homeland, and the FBI will keep fighting for America's businesses and economic security," said Roman Rozhavsky, an assistant director of the FBI's counterintelligence and espionage division.
It was not immediately clear on Friday whether Liu was being represented by an attorney. According to court records, Lui has not yet pleaded guilty or not guilty to the charges.
In a 22-page indictment, prosecutors said Liu worked with several co-conspirators who operated shell companies to first get the chips to either Malaysia or Singapore, and then into China.
Prosecutors said a company owned by Liu served as a go-between for foreign shipping companies and US chip manufacturers, and that Liu lied to US companies, claiming the chips wouldn't end up in China.
The operation began in 2023 and continued until August, according to the indictment. Liu's company was paid over $180 million by Malaysian shipping companies to broker the chip deals, prosecutors said.
If convicted of all charges, Liu could serve a combined 50 years in prison.
"This case shows yet again that smuggling is a losing proposition — legally, economically and technically," an Nvidia spokesperson said in a statement. "Our work with law enforcement has led to prosecutions, and we will continue to engage with law enforcement."

The official cause of death for Fiona Lowe, the 13-year-old daughter of actor Chad Lowe and niece of Rob Lowe, has been revealed.
The database for the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner confirmed that Fiona Lowe died Tuesday by suicide and died in a hospital. Chad Lowe, the Emmy-winning star of “Life Goes On,” and his family announced Fiona’s death in a statement shared with People on Tuesday. The actor shares Fiona and two other daughters with wife Kim Painter.
Before the medical examiner’s report became public, Lowe’s family did not reveal a cause of death but in its statement mentioned contact information for a mental health lifeline. The family in its statement said it was “heartbroken by the loss” and remembered Fiona as a “loving girl who was smart, creative, and loved to dance.”
The family of ‘Life Goes On’ star Chad Lowe announces the death of 13-year-old daughter Fiona. ‘She was the light of our lives,’ the family wrote and included information for a mental health lifeline.
“She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents. In fact, she was the light of our lives,” the family added. Lowe and his loved ones also said Fiona’s death is “devastating for our entire family” and asked for prayers and privacy.
Fiona’s death comes after the “Pretty Little Liars” actor’s family lost their home in the Palisades fire, which killed 12 peopleand consumed more than 6,500 structures. He shared videos and photos of the destruction to his Instagram page.
Lowe, 58, is the younger brother of actor Rob Lowe. He and Painter married in 2010 and welcomed Fiona in 2012. Fiona celebrated her 13th birthday in November and was the second of the couple’s three daughters. Lowe and Painter first welcomed daughter Mabel in 2009 and their youngest daughter, Nixie, in 2016.

articles.title_orig: A Cross-Border Problem: Modeling New World Screwworm’s South American Range
articles.title_zh: A Cross-Border Problem: Modeling New World Screwworm’s South American Range
articles.content_orig:
Traumatic myiasis is about as gross as it gets.
A gravid New World screwworm fly ( Cochliomyia hominivorax ) lumbers through the air, looking for the perfect place to deposit her heavy burden of eggs—maybe an open wound or an exposed mucus membrane. Eventually, they’ll hatch out tiny maggots, each sporting a treacherous spiral of backwards-facing spines. These will anchor the maggots as they use razor-sharp mouth hooks to burrow and tear into tender living tissue.
Historically, New World screwworm has been considered a livestock issue, affecting domesticated animals like cattle, sheep, and goats. But a wide range of warm-blooded animals can be hosts—including wildlife, household pets, and even humans.
That’s one takeaway from a recent study, published in August in the Journal of Medical Entomology , that applied a One Health approach to modeling New World screwworm distribution across South America. The team comprised disease experts, data analysts, entomologists, and veterinarians from institutions in Chile, Paraguay, and Venezuela.
“We all knew the fly affects livestock, but as we went through the literature, we came across cases in wildlife, such as maned wolves, giant otters, ocelots, lesser grisons, and wild boars,” says lead author Marlon Mauricio Ardila, a Ph.D. student at Chile’s Universidad de Concepción. “And that’s when you grasp the real problem. Those wild populations are completely outside the reach of any veterinary control, so they act as a reservoir that can keep the cycle going—even when you think you’ve already brought the fly under control in livestock.”
New World screwworm once affected a large swath of the Americas, from the southern United States through central Argentina. A program utilizing the sterile insect technique began in the 1950s and continued through the turn of the century to eradicate the fly in the U.S., Mexico, and central America. But it has returned to Central America in the past couple of years, reaching the U.S. this summer. All the while, populations remained strong in South America. But co-author Leidi Herrera of the Universidad Nacional de Asunción, Paraguay, and the Universidad Central de Venezuela says population data was limited.
“My research into metaxenic diseases and zoonoses … revealed significant gaps in surveillance in our region,” she says. “Although screwworm myiasis has a severe impact on health and the economy in Latin America, studies in South America were scarce.”
Existing models mainly looked at Argentina and Chile plus some nation-level analysis in some other South American countries. Now, the team wanted to model the distribution of New World screwworm for the entire region, with a strong focus on finding environmental conditions that might lead the flies to persist or disperse.
To do this, they used modeling tools along with records of New World screwworm myiasis cases in humans and other warm-blooded animals across nine geographic areas. The data included cases of more than 9,000 New World screwworm larvae, which broke out to about 38% involving human myiasis and nearly 62% involving non-human animals or unspecified myiasis.
This ecological modeling found that temperature and rainfall heavily influence the distribution of New World screwworm in South America—especially winter thermal stress. It turns out screwworm larvae and pupae don’t do well when the temperature dips to its lowest seasonal extreme. They also struggle when the temperature during the day is unstable, which is known to affect how well insects do normal things like fly, mate, and lay eggs.
The models also predict that some places—like the humid lowlands of eastern Paraguay, northeastern Brazil, and parts of the Amazon basin—have exactly what New World screwworm need to thrive: sufficient moisture so their pupae don’t dry out and plenty of opportunities for the flies to find vulnerable (and ostensibly tasty) wounds.
The team used epidemiological records to confirm and extend the models.
Overall, the team say that this problem is one that combines issues of the environment, animal health, and public health—and therefore requires an integrated approach to surveilling and responding to the threat.
“This is a starting point, not the end,” says Ardila. “For now, the paper calls for strengthening surveillance, training producers, and coordinating control across countries—because this is a cross-border problem.”
It also leaves many questions still open: confirming how wildlife act as a reservoir, figuring out the genetic barrier that prevents the flies from taking up areas that seem perfect from a climate perspective, and looking at how other flies that cause myiasis overlap New World screwworm . Herrera says they’re seeking partnerships and funding to design integrated monitoring tools and control strategies.
One thing is certain: It’s work that needs to be done together.
“ Presence and distribution of Cochliomyia hominivorax (Diptera: Calliphoridae) in South America: ecological niche modeling and epidemiological implications under the One Health approach ”

articles.title_orig: Egor Kornev Delivers 44.84 100 Freestyle To Match Kyle Chalmers’ World Record
articles.title_zh: Egor Kornev Delivers 44.84 100 Freestyle To Match Kyle Chalmers’ World Record
articles.content_orig:
22-year-old Egor Kornev crushed a lifetime best of 44.84 to win the men's 100m freestyle in Baku, matching Aussie Kyle Chalmers as the fastest performer ever. Archive photo via Mickael Malaper/ Malaper Photography
October 02nd, 2026 Europe , International , News , Previews & Recaps , Records , Swimming World Cup Series
Day two of the first stop of the 2026 World Aquatics Swimming World Cup taking place in Baku brought us our first World-Record-equalling performance of the series.
Racing in the final of the men’s 100m freestyle tonight, and only a handful of events after his 50m back World Cup record , 22-year-old Egor Kornev of Russia busted out a time of 44.84 to take the gold.
Kornev’s time exactly matched the current World Record of 44.84 Australian Olympic champion Kyle Chalmers put on the books at the 2021 edition of the World Cup in Kazan. That time also stands as the World Cup record.
Entering this competition, Kornev’s fastest 100m freestyle result rested at the 44.99 he established in 2025, with that former PB representing his only other outing under the 45-second barrier. It came within .05 of the Russian record of 44.95 retired Olympian Vlad Morozov turned in during the 2018 World Cup, so Kornev now owns that standard as well.
Tonight, Kornev opened in 21.62 and brought it home in 23.22, which is a slightly different tactic than Chalmers, where the Aussie was .22 quicker to start out.
Runner-up status this evening went to LCM 50 freestyle Olympic champion and World Record holder Cameron McEvoy of Australia, who registered 45.36 followed by Russian Vasilii Kukushkin , who bagged bronze in 46.77.
As for new father McEvoy, the 32-year-old 50m freestyle specialist has only begun training for the 100m as of August of last year.
He told World Aquatics he will be using each World Cup stop to test a different approach to the race.
“[There are] three different race strategies I’m testing out,” he explained.
“That’s going to give me so much data. Then I kind of cherry-pick all the good stuff, and then hopefully the Worlds is the best of the lot.
“I’ve seen many people who have a lot of top-end speed and they go out a little bit too hard and then that last 25 [metres] it hits,” he said.
“But in general I’m excited for it. I want to beat my PB from the past, 46.1. If I do that, I think that’d be good.” (World Aquatics)
Is it wrong that for me the biggest story here is Cam 45.36?
He will crush this WR multiple times. It is clear
Kyle’s time as WR holder is running out.
With a faster reaction time (he was .70 off the blocks, .10 slower than McEvoy), he would’ve cleared it.
“If my grandma had wheels, she’d have been a bike” type comment

articles.title_orig: Clay Travis: inside the Maga permadad’s world of sports bros, trans panic and mortgages
articles.title_zh: Clay Travis: inside the Maga permadad’s world of sports bros, trans panic and mortgages
articles.content_orig:
The rightwing media mogul has lost ground to the likes of Pat McAfee and Joe Rogan. He’s hoping his new venture can recapture some headway
W hen Maga media blowhard Clay Travis offered $2m to Colin Kaepernick last week to appear on the daily talkshow he hosts with former CIA analyst Buck Sexton, it represented the culmination of a years-long obsession on the right with the onetime NFL star. In Travis’s telling of history, Kaepernick taking a knee during the 2016 NFL season was the event that catalyzed professional sports into the era of “woke” excess from which, he claims, it has been struggling to recover ever since.
But more than simply confirming the right’s longstanding villainization of Kaepernick, Travis’s offer was also a smarmy bid for publicity for his new media venture, Sport & State. Sport & State, which launched in August, is Travis’s bid to get back to his roots as a media mogul who sold the wildly popular Outkick to Fox Sports for a rumored $100m, and reclaim some of the cultural territory lost to fellow sports bros and Magagitators like Pat McAfee, Joe Rogan, Tucker Carlson and Ben Shapiro. But if there’s one thing Sport & State won’t be doing, it’s engaging with anyone beyond the Magaverse. There has been no response from Kaepernick since Travis made his “offer” of $2m to charity in exchange for an interview, which suggests he understands that it was extended more in a spirit of trolling buffoonery than sincerity. No one associated with the left or progressive politics ever appears on Travis’s shows, for the simple reason that they are designed purely for the right to talk to itself. (Some would say the same could be said of the left, although the disregard for dissenting perspectives in the Magasphere seems way more extreme.) More than it heralds a renewal of Travis’s career or an injection of fresh energy into the Trumpist mediasphere, Sport & State is a case study in the stagnation that has taken hold on the right as Donald Trump stares down the barrel of defeat in November’s midterm elections.
Having spent the better part of the past two months listening to the Clay Travis & Buck Sexton Show (which runs from noon to 3pm ET every weekday) and the Clay Travis Show (3-4pm), I can say with confidence that there are, in essence, only 11 topics a given day’s programming on Sport & State will cover: college football gambling picks; Trumpworld figures who are friends with Travis and Sexton; the wonderful job that these figures are doing in power (sometimes mixed with the preceding theme: “Our friend Kash, who is truly our friend, Clay and I are both buddies with him, he’s a good man,” Sexton affirmed on a recent episode); the low levels of testosterone apparently common among white males who voted for Kamala Harris in 2024 (“white dudes for Kamala” is perhaps the gravest slur on the Clay Travis Show); trans women in professional sport (I haven’t calculated this precisely but at a guess I’d say this accounts for 20% to 50% of the discussion on any show that Travis hosts, even as the number of actual trans women competing in professional American sports remains exactly zero and there are probably fewer than 10 trans athletes in total in college sports); crime in America’s cities (in recent weeks the fixation has been Lindsay Clancy , but it’s liable to switch at any moment to Iryna Zarutska, Luigi Mangione, Charlie Kirk, Iryna Zarutska , or whatever murder happens to have taken place on that particular day in New York City); the problem with women (in summary: they are women); the fact that Travis and Sexton are both family men with wives and children; the fact that Travis has a law degree from Vanderbilt University; the fact that Travis studied law at Vanderbilt after he was rejected by Stanford (“I wanted to go to Stanford Law School, they didn’t want me, I went to Vanderbilt instead – I’ve now made a $10m donation to Vanderbilt Law School”); and the fact that Travis appeared on Fox News last night and will appear on Fox News again later today. Sprinkled throughout all of this are plugs for Hard Rock Bet (“Bet $5, get $100 in bonus bets”), which is the official gambling partner of Sport & State and holds equity in Travis’s upstart media concern, and companies such as Perfect 10 Mortgage, Crockett Coffee, XX-XY Athletics and Clay Travis Law, all of which – it should come as no surprise – Travis either outright owns or holds a stake in.
The recursiveness and self-referentiality of the advertising and content on Sport & State are all part of the site’s commercial strategy, according to Travis’s lengthy mission statement . The onshoring of all the advertising will, Travis claims, insulate his new venture from the vagaries of media’s traditional dependence on subscriptions and external advertisers. Gambling is the key revenue driver: Outkick became an affiliate of FanDuel after sports betting was legalized in 2018 and eventually made $350 for every new gambling account it helped set up, netting $2m in affiliate betting revenue on Super Bowl Sunday in 2021 alone, and Sport & State is set up to reap similar rewards through its partnership with Hard Rock Bet. But Travis’s expectation is that his home loan business, say, will also prosper as viewers stay online to hear his views on Ole Miss v LSU, Lane Kiffin or the apparent attempted hijacking of the Israel-bound passenger jet and what it means for the future of DEI in America.
Inadvertently, perhaps, Travis’s sidequest companies offer a sense of what Sport & State’s ideal audience member looks like: a patriotic American male with a habit of deploying the phrase “perfect 10” unironically whose life revolves around mortgages, coffee, litigation, gambling and moaning about trans women. On the Crockett Coffee blog , recent posts include “American Coffee Origins and Brewing Techniques”, “Discovering American Coffee’s Unique Flavors”, and “The Americano: A Complete History” (do I detect a theme here?); Travis sips throughout the day on Sport & State from a black spillproof coffee container, emphasizing his own commitment to the cause of caffeine and country.
If there’s a persistent “ Spider-Men pointing at each other ” quality to the advertising on Sport & State, that extends to the content as well. Travis’s big idea is that in the age of AI and commodified writing, it’s better to go deep than big, that depth of audience commitment matters more than the old traffic era’s scale-focused contest for clicks. There may be some wisdom in the strategy, but that approach – drumming down and appeasing an already loyal base – seems to have become the media-obsessed Trump White House’s guiding political strategy too, a choice that risks self-sabotage as the midterms loom. Travis’s theory of media is second-term Trump’s theory of power: instead of growing the audience, the electorate, the constituency, the sole purpose of having attention is to give those listening more of the same. Discussion on Sport & State this week included a summary of Travis and Sexton’s Monday meeting with Trump in the Oval Office. Their main point was to emphasize that “President Trump says he loves the show, says we’re doing a great job” and that various Trumpworld figures greeted them during their half-hour in front of the Resolute Desk. “We saw Karoline Leavitt, our very good friend”; “We also saw Susie Wiles – she said she is cancer-free now”; “We got a little quick high-five from Stephen Miller”.
Over a chyron announcing THE VOICE OF SEAN HANNITY, the longtime Fox News host then called in to discuss: sports betting (what else?); the border collie he’s about to take delivery of at the conclusion of nine months of dog training (if this is what it takes to survive domestic cohabitation with Hannity as an animal, imagine how things must be for the humans in his house); Gavin Newsom and Kathy Hochul as the highest-taxing, and therefore worst, governors in America; and potential Democratic candidates for 2028 (Hannity thinks AOC will be

articles.title_orig: Weak jobs report is yet another headwind for Trump and Republicans ahead of midterms
articles.title_zh: Weak jobs report is yet another headwind for Trump and Republicans ahead of midterms
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
September's weak jobs report was the last reading on the labor market before the midterm elections, and the weak figures will further complicate the job facing President Trump and Republicans to sell voters on their economic record.
The president and his party have already been grappling with an economic message that is failing to gain traction, as polls show voters are deeply unhappy about the economic trajectory one month out from Election Day.
US payrolls rose by just 29,000 jobs in September after 90,000 had been expected. Wage growth also cooled, another significant figure underscoring Americans' worries about their purchasing power amid persistent inflation.
Average hourly earnings rose just 0.1% in September and are up 3% over the entire year. That's below the 3.4% rate of inflation over that same period.
Friday's release also showed that the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2%, and July and August payroll numbers were revised downward, further clouding the economic picture.
Read more: Credit card vs. savings: What to use when you're unemployed
Allianz chief economic adviser Mohamed El-Erian told Yahoo Finance on Friday that economic pressures have a pronounced effect on lower-income households.
"It's not just an economic worry. It's a social and political worry as well," El-Erian said.
Democrats were quick to tout the number as an indictment of Trump's economic record, while the White House and Republicans highlighted specific facets of the report to paint a more positive picture.
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said in television interviews that he was "not even a little bit" disappointed by the number and that the US economy was being realigned. He acknowledged that the latest number was a "little bit lukewarm," but said that monthly job figures "bounce up and down."
Hassett and other White House officials, like Deputy Press Secretary Taylor Rogers, also focused on increasing labor force participation and pointed out that the government shed 17,000 jobs last month as private payrolls gained 46,000, although that latter figure was still below expectations.
Rogers noted that over 1 million private-sector jobs have now been created during Trump's second term.
Trump, meanwhile, continued to tout his economic message Friday, posting about investments from South Korea (even amid questions about whether South Korea was actually on board with the plan ).
The president is set to crisscross the country in the coming weeks to sell his economic record.
His message, as the election enters its final stretch to Nov. 3, is that the economy is in a "golden age" and the main issue is that he and his fellow Republicans have "done a very bad job of explaining."
Democrats, meanwhile, put the number in election-year terms. Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts calculated that Trump's economy has added an average of 33,000 jobs a month since Inauguration Day in 2025 — "far below the 120,000-a-month average in 2024" of the last year of former President Joe Biden's time in office, she said.
Like other Democrats, Warren also zeroed in on weak wage growth, writing that "since the start of Trump's war [in Iran], real wages have fallen."
Gbenga Ajilore, chief economist at the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities and a former Biden administration official, added that "this is an okay reading for the labor market, but in the broader context, lower wage growth is a warning sign given the administration's harmful policies."
The latest release also comes as countless polls have shown Trump and Republicans deeply underwater on the economy, an area of intense focus among voters . A compilation of recent polls from Silver Bulletin shows an aggregate 65% disapproval rating of Trump on the economy , versus just 31.4% approval.
The numbers are even worse on inflation: 74.3% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of inflation, while just 22.6% approve.
This story has been updated.
Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title_orig: Affordable Alternatives To Apple's AirPods Max
articles.title_zh: Affordable Alternatives To Apple's AirPods Max
articles.content_orig:
If you can live without deep iOS integration and the polished design, you could save hundreds.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
If you're willing to pay for them, there's a lot to like about the AirPods Max . You get a dose of high-end design with deep iOS integration and smart features like Personalized Spatial Audio, Adaptive EQ, Live Translation, Adaptive Audio and Conversation Awareness. There's also lossless audio over USB-C, if you're into that sort of thing, but it's more common on spec sheets these days.
Of course, the main drawback with the AirPods Max has always been the price. At $549, the headphones rank among the most expensive sets we've reviewed. But if you're willing to give up some features, namely the tools that can only be used with Apple devices, you can save a significant sum without sacrificing too much performance.
Currently being tested for review.
At $200, the Space 2 Pro will cost you less than half of a pair of the AirPods Max 2. And yes, you will need to make some sacrifices to save that much dough. First and foremost, you'll give up the deep integration with iOS and Apple devices that the AirPods Max offers. You'll also have to forego the premium design for something that's still refined, but also decidedly plastic. If neither of those are dealbreakers, then there's plenty to like about the Space 2 Pro.
This most is Anker's first Soundcore headphones with its Thus AI chip inside. The component is responsible for active noise cancellation (ANC), voice quality (on both calls and for voice controls) and HearID customized sound. The ANC setup, which also utilizes eight sensors, does a decent job with human voices and constant noise sources. Voice quality is great, thanks in part to that chip and a six-microphone configuration, but you will notice some slight degradation when the system kicks in to block background noise. And the stock tuning offers crisp highs and deep low-end tone right out of the box.
The benefit of all that plastic is the Space 2 Pro is very light, so it's comfortable to wear for extended periods of time. These headphones also have intuitive physical controls that are reliable and easy to use instead of touch panels for swipes and taps. Multipoint Bluetooth and 30 hours of battery life (ANC on) are also on the spec sheet.
$359 is still a big chunk of change, but in the case of the second-gen QuietComfort Headphones, you're paying for Bose's noise-blocking prowess. The overall sound quality here is nice too, though the company's own Ultra model does better. On these "regular" QC headphones, you get Cinema Mode and Immersive Audio, the latter of which is the company's take on spatial sound. The QuietComfort Headphones are no slouch, and you'll be plenty pleased with the performance after saving nearly $200 over the AirPods Max 2.
Read our full review here.
At this point, you've likely seen someone wearing the AirPods Max 2 during a workout. Those headphones aren't a great choice for sweaty activities since the ear pads are made of "a breathable mesh textile." Beats headphones haven't been engineered to withstand sweat either, but they were also popular among gym goers and athletes. With the Beats 360 though, Apple finally has a set of fitness headphones in its lineup with IPX4 sweat resistance.
Since Beats is owned by Apple, you get a lot of the AirPods Max benefits here. Those include one-touch pairing, automatic switching between Apple devices on your iCloud account, Audio Sharing with compatible earbuds/headphones, Find My compatibility and hands-free access to Siri. The Beats 360 lasts for up to 12 hours longer than the AirPods Max 2 (ANC enabled) and there's the ability to swap out both the ear and headband cushions. Plus, Beats' affinity for bass will help keep your energy up during a workout, but it's not as overbearing as was on the company's early models.
If you want a good set of headphones for under $100, you have to make a lot of sacrifices. However, sound quality, battery life and comfort don't have to be on that list. With Audio-Technica's M20xBT, you get a classic design and the company's warm, inviting sound quality. 60-hour battery life is excellent and the headphones are lightweight and very comfy. What you won't find here is ANC, but basics like multipoint Bluetooth and optional wired use are still available.
When the comparison device is $549, a $299 set is significantly more affordable. In this case, that's the price of the Fender Mix: a set of noise-cancelling headphones that debuted just before CES. The new line of audio devices comes from Fender Audio, a collaboration of the Fender Corporation (of guitar fame) and Riffsound. The result is a cleverly designed set of headphones with a stored lossless Bluetooth dongle and replaceable battery. There's also a crisp, detailed quality to the sound that I really enjoyed. Plus, the company now has an app for settings changes, a key element that was missing during my review.
The five-way joystick controls are pleasant to use and 52 hours of battery life with ANC enabled is a big perk. Speaking of noise cancellation, the performance is respectable here, though it's not on the level of Bose and some others. Still, it's enough to block mild-to-moderate distractions.
Skullcandy Crusher 1080: Haptic bass is the main draw here, but the ANC performance and overall audio quality don't overcome the bulky, dated design.
JBL Live 780NC: This model is comfortable to wear with lots of features and solid active noise cancellation, but the overall sound quality is underwhelming and call quality isn't great either.
Sony WH-1000XM4C: This is still a solid set of headphones six years later, but Sony's reboot doesn't offer enough to justify the $300 price tag.
Sony WH-1000XM6: The best headphones you can buy right now will only save you $99 over the AirPods Max 2. That's not nothing, but it's also not enough in our book to name it an affordable alternative.
Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd gen): This is the best ANC performance you'll find, but at $449, these headphones don't fit the description of an affordable alternative either.
Sennheiser HDB 630: I really like the sound quality on these headphones, especially with the lossless audio capabilities. But at $500, these don't offer much savings over the AirPods Max 2.
Sennheiser Momentum 5: Sennheiser's well-rounded over-ear headphones are no slouch. The main issue that kept them off of this list is the $400 price.
Sonos Ace: Sonos' original headphones are now just $350 following the debut of the Ace Ultra. But unless you also have a Sonos soundbar, these aren't a very compelling alternative for everyday use.
When Engadget compiles buyer's guides like these, we initially draw on our decades of product review expertise. Throughout each year, we review well over 100 new devices, which gives us a solid foundation for selecting the best products that fit any given criteria. For this guide specifically, I was able to revisit recently reviewed devices as a refresher, re-familiarize myself with the products on my initial short list and make the best selections based on the affordable alternatives criteria. I write almost all of the headphone reviews at Engadget, and edit those I don't write, so I have a deep knowledge of this particular category.
We may update our selections as needed, after new products are announced and reviewed.

articles.title_orig: World News in Brief: Cycle of violence continues in Haiti, seafarer deaths off Somalia, food insecurity in the Middle East
articles.title_zh: World News in Brief: Cycle of violence continues in Haiti, seafarer deaths off Somalia, food insecurity in the Middle East
articles.content_orig:
Facebook Twitter Print Email
Haitians remain in the grip of lethal gang violence as it continues to “adapt and expand”, the UN’s top rights official, Volker Türk, said on Friday.
In an update to the Human Rights Council , the High Commissioner welcomed the first Gang Suppression Force operations, mandated by the UN Security Council .
These will help boost security in Haiti “but the Force remains far below the strength needed”, Mr. Türk insisted, in support of its “full, accelerated deployment” with human rights safeguards embedded.
At least 5,700 people have been confirmed killed or injured by gangs – or during operations against them – since 1 January, according to the UN human rights office, OHCHR .
Gang members have also kidnapped more than 230 people and raped at least 1,000 women and girls. The real figures are likely much higher, Mr. Türk said.
In his update, the High Commissioner for Human Rights also warned that “extortion, looting and destruction of property” are crippling economic activity in Haiti.
The “constant danger” prevents people from reaching schools, hospitals, and essential services, Mr. Türk stressed.
Three hijacked ships have been freed after months in captivity, but five seafarers died during the rescue of one of them, the head of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) has said.
IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez offered his condolences after the operation to free the HONOUR 25 in Somali waters on 29 September, in which several other crew members were seriously injured.
Mr. Dominguez said seafarers “should not have to lose their lives for the service they provide for the world”, and called for renewed resolve, targeted cooperation and the resources needed to stop piracy in the region.
The HONOUR 25 was one of three vessels released this week, along with the SEAMULL (also known as SIBU 1) and the MT EUREKA, all seized between April and August by pirates and armed robbers.
In total, 44 seafarers were freed and their governments are working to arrange their repatriation. Mr. Dominguez thanked Somalia's Government for its efforts, but noted that 22 seafarers remain captive aboard the ASANA.
He urged Governments to bring new initiatives, such as the proposed Group of Friends of Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers, to the IMO, and stressed the importance of the EUNAVFOR Aspides and Atalanta operations for maritime security in the region.
An additional 11.7 million women and girls in 28 countries could face food insecurity by the end of the year due to the escalating conflict in the Middle East and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
These crises are driving up food prices and putting a strain on livelihoods and household resources, UN Women said in new analysis published on Friday.
Presenting the findings to journalists in Geneva, UN Women Deputy Executive Director Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvanda said the estimates are a potential scenario, not a forecast, and that the number is in addition to the 208 million women and girls who were already estimated to be food insecure or malnourished in these countries.
“Experience from past conflicts shows that when food is scarce, women often reduce the amount they eat or skip meals so that children and other family members can eat,” she said.
The greatest numbers of women and girls at risk are in populous countries, while South Sudan, Sudan, Haiti, Yemen and Palestine face the highest concentration of overlapping vulnerabilities.
UN Women recommends linking food and cash assistance to nutrition, protection, employment and agricultural services. Women should also have access to land, credit and productive resources.
The agency also highlighted the need for better collection of data that shows where food insecurity is worsening and who is eating less, losing income and carrying the heaviest burden of unpaid care work.

articles.title_orig: G7 countries to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil reserves
articles.title_zh: G7 countries to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil reserves
articles.content_orig:
Member countries in the Group of Seven agreed Friday to release tens of millions of barrels of diesel fuel and crude oil, the latest move by industrial economies around the world to cap soaring gas prices.
Following a G7 videoconference hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron, President Donald Trump said, “Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil.”
“The process will begin immediately,” Trump posted on Truth Social.
Gas prices have soared since the United States and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28. But diesel in particular saw a renewed surge this summer after the Russia-Ukraine war escalated in July. Since late February, the average price of U.S. diesel has surged 70% to $6.37 per gallon.
The release will be as much as 100 million barrels over the course of four months, the G7 said in a statement. It noted that there would be a “substantial diesel release within the first 20 days.”
The leaders also said that they would begin coordinating maintenance schedules for oil refineries in their respective countries, “to prevent simultaneous capacity shutdowns and temporarily increase utilization rates where feasible.”
Many American and European refiners are already operating at maximum capacity levels.
“Our citizens’ concerns about energy prices remain a top priority,” the group said.
Oil analyst Andy Lipow said the release could help smooth over recent supply disruptions.
“A release of 100 million barrels of diesel fuel over four months would essentially replace Russian exports which have been banned as Ukrainian drone strikes have severely reduced Russian refining capacity,” said Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates.
At the gas pump, he said, “A release of this magnitude could temporarily reduce diesel prices by 25 cents per gallon but does little to increase refinery capacity to produce more.”
In March, countries that are members of the International Energy Agency approved a release of 400 million barrels of crude oil. That helped to partially ease the energy supply crunch for a time, but prices continued to rise.
As of Friday, prices still remain sharply elevated since the Iran war began. Brent crude oil, which was down 3% in anticipation of the news, still hovered above $100 per barrel. Since the start of the year, Brent prices are up more than 60% still.
The agreement between G7 countries also comes after a weeklong pressure campaign by the Trump administration on its European allies, particularly Germany and France, which hold a large share of the European Union’s diesel reserves.
“American farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage” alone, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote on X late Thursday.
With just weeks to go until the Nov. 3 midterm elections, Republicans are facing a wall of poor polling numbers on the economy.
Just 41% of registered voters approve of Trump’s handling of the U.S. economy, according to the most recent NBC News polling, while 56% disapprove.
Meanwhile, economists say Trump’s policies are fueling inflation, roiling financial markets and upending global trade.
Against this backdrop, the president and his party were eager for  a development like Friday’s G-7 agreement to help show the public they could make progress on a central election issue: Sky-high gas prices.
But at the same time as Trump is hailing the release of oil and diesel reserves, he has also been openly considering a U.S. diesel export ban.
This would hit E.U. countries, as well as the United Kingdom, particularly hard.
Earlier Friday, the E.U. said it “fully rejects any ban on diesel.”
“A ban would not be beneficial to anyone,” a European Commission spokeswoman told reporters in a briefing.
Following the G7 leaders’ announcement, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said they “welcome the decision of G7 countries not to impose any export bans on allies and the continued solidarity between partners.”
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.

articles.title_orig: The Inner Circle 33 Main Event Result: Regian Eersel Survives Early Scare, Stops George Jarvis To Retain World Title
articles.title_zh: The Inner Circle 33 Main Event Result: Regian Eersel Survives Early Scare, Stops George Jarvis To Retain World Title
articles.content_orig:
Two-sport ONE World Champion Regian “The Immortal” Eersel has built a career defined by overcoming adversity, and the main event of The Inner Circle 33 on Friday, October 2 was no different.
The Surinamese superstar walked the tightrope between glory and disaster before retaining his ONE Lightweight Muay Thai World Title against Englishman George “G-Unit” Jarvis via knockout. Their high-stakes rematch streamed exclusively for subscribers at live.onefc.com in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s iconic Lumpinee Stadium.
With the memory of being stopped in just 84 seconds still fresh, Jarvis arrived with a tighter guard and sharper feints to disguise his attack. Eersel, who vowed the outcome would mirror their first meeting , welcomed the chaos and fired back with a sharp one-two before going airborne with a flying knee.
Despite being busted open, Jarvis absorbed the damage and bided his time, eventually uncorking a massive left hook to the temple that sent the defending king crashing to the canvas.
Eersel survived to the bell, and the Sityodtong Amsterdam affiliate deployed leg kicks from the outside in the second canto. On the flip side, Jarvis, growing bolder, began swinging with real venom behind his punches. Sensing his foe’s guard hanging low in the heat of the exchange, “The Immortal” stayed patient and dropped the challenger with a pinpoint left hook to the chin.
Even at one knockdown apiece, neither man backed off once the third round began. The Surinamese martial arts hero, who also holds the ONE Lightweight Kickboxing World Title, worked behind a steady jab and extended combinations.
“G-Unit,” on the other hand, bit down and fired back with heavy hooks upstairs and to the body. Experience proved the difference, however, as the kingpin began targeting Jarvis’ swelling right eye with piercing straights, the damage mounting with every exchange.
Jarvis then opened the fourth with his signature left cross as Eersel peppered him with head kicks from the outside. Reading the first signs of fatigue, the Amsterdam-based star abandoned the kicks and returned to the target that had already done so much damage, landing another clean left hook that sent Jarvis down for a second time.
“G-Unit” immediately covered his right eye, and the referee called a halt to the pulsating war at 1:39 of round four.
The win marked yet another defining chapter in Eersel’s reign, extending his ONE Lightweight Muay Thai World Title defenses to four and improving his career record to 66-5.
It also made “‘The Immortal” the most successful titleholder in ONE Championship history, a 12-time World Champion across both Muay Thai and kickboxing.

articles.title_orig: Gino’s Pizza Place owner is old guard in a new world
articles.title_zh: Gino’s Pizza Place owner is old guard in a new world
articles.content_orig:
Gino has proudly served the Tonawanda community from 351 Fries Road since opening his doors in 1983.
Now in his fourth decade of making pizza at his eponymous restaurant in Tonawanda, Gino Pinzone is a part of the old guard who made Buffalo pizza a thing. At seventy years old, he still gets behind the counter of Gino’s Pizza Place at 9 a.m. to make dough, prep sauce, and mentor a new generation of employees.
You’ve been a fixture in the local food scene for decades. Where did that passion for cooking begin?
Everything started back in Sicily. My mother had eleven children, so she worked at home day and night, night and day, constantly cooking for fourteen people. I’m number eight, so I did a lot of helping, making everything you could possibly make at home. I still do it for myself today. I learned everything from her.
Did she teach you to bake?
In those days, we really could not afford meat. Bread was everything. Chinese people use rice. Mexicans use tortilla shells. We were heavy on bread. When it came out of the oven, it was a treat just to put extra virgin olive oil and black pepper on it. That was it.
How did you end up owning a pizzeria?
I went to Buffalo State for Industrial Arts; I was going to be a teacher. But in 1978, my older brother opened a pizzeria and asked me and my brother Frank to work for him. I liked it a lot. I never finished my master's degree in teaching because I was doing okay making pizzas with my brother! I opened my first solo place in November 1983, and here I am today.
What do you love the most?
My employees. Some started as high school students from across the street. They start folding boxes and then, little by little, I teach them how to do a few things here and there. They might go away for college, but they always come back. It’s rewarding. Take care of the employees because the employees will always take care of you. And that’s what they do. I trust them, and they do a great job.
It sounds almost like a family atmosphere .
I get kids coming in who might be a little quiet or shy. Their parents ask if I can hire them, to get them out of their bedrooms and away from the video games. Next thing you know, they’re hopping around and working and loving it. I tell them, “You’re learning a skill.”
It’s not just about making pizzas but also learning how to get around a restaurant. You need to do dishes, you need to cut celery, you need to do this... Even if they graduate and get a degree, they can go anywhere in the world and work in a pizzeria because they know how a kitchen moves.
Many of the restaurant’s Instagram reels feature you. Do you enjoy being in the spotlight?
[Laughs] My son Phil does all that! He puts the camera in my face and says, “Dad, we’re introducing eggplant pizza today.” I always tell him, “Phil, I’m not doing a second take.” Whatever comes out of me, comes out. We did one video recently that had 20,000 viewers. People come in now just because they want to see me and talk to me.
Why have you never expanded to a second location?
I want to be totally responsible for everything that comes out of the place. I do all the prep work. I’m there from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. every day. On Fridays, I’m there until dinner is over. On Sundays, I’m there until the Bills game is over.  Nobody does it like the owner. It’s hard to train somebody to do things the way I do. Nowadays, people open five places and there’s no personal feeling.
And after forty years, most people would be taking it easy. What keeps you coming back every morning?
It’s not the money. It’s the DNA of a pizza guy in me. I see regulars who came in as kids now bringing their own grandkids in and putting them up on my counter. Why would I walk away? It makes it all worthwhile.

articles.content_orig:
REBROADCAST: Texas Marching Classic
Massive drum corps news just dropped.
DCI Open Class veterans Gold and The Battalion have both been approved to transition into the World Class beginning with the 2027 DCI Summer Tour.
All of the Bands Competing at the 2027 Texas Marching Classic 🤠   | BOA Weekend Watch Guide, Oct. 3 🗓️   | Troopers Announce DCI 2027 Show Title 👀   | Recent Marching Headlines You May Have Missed 🔥   | WATCH LIVE on October 17: Texas Marching Classic 🤠
After a successful vote by DCI's member organizations in addition to a multi-year examination of the organizations' finances and operations, both Gold and The Battalion are excited to endeavor on a new adventure in their new class.
A recent success story of the transition from Open Class to World Class is Spartans, which just completed its first full season as a DCI World Class member with their show, 'On the World Stage.'
Here's what the two ensembles had to say to DCI about the move:
“This is a culmination of everything we’ve been building over the last 12 years. For our staff and members, there’s definitely excitement, but I think it will mostly feel like a natural next step, because we’ve always seen ourselves as headed in this direction. We’ve been incredibly honored by the new fans we’ve met on the road as our tours have grown longer each year. We’re excited to grow that community as we take this step.” - Tyler Hess, director of The Battalion
“Moving into World Class is a big moment for Gold. It’s something we’ve been working toward for a long time, even if it wasn’t always the immediate goal in front of us. We’ve always worked hard to make drum corps accessible and to create a place where members can grow as performers and as people. That remains important to us regardless of what classification we compete in.” - Kevin Valentine, executive director of Gold
To read DCI's full press release, click here.
The Battalion had a breakout year, earning the silver medal at DCI Open Class World Championships (81.500) and 20th at DCI World Championship Semifinals (79.225).
Gold finished out the 2026 DCI season placing third at DCI Open Class World Championships (80.300) and 22nd at DCI World Championship Semifinals (77.975).

articles.title_orig: The 7-year-old Nvidia Shield TV is now $100 more expensive thanks to AI
articles.title_zh: The 7-year-old Nvidia Shield TV is now $100 more expensive thanks to AI
articles.content_orig:
The era of generative AI has upended technology supply chains, and there is one ironclad rule in 2026: If it has memory or storage, it’s getting more expensive. Even devices with years-old tech inside are still apparently subject to that unwritten rule. Nvidia has just announced that the Shield TV Pro is getting $100 more expensive, effective immediately.
The most recent version of the Shield streaming box debuted in 2019, running Android TV with AI upscaling and hardware decoding for almost any type of media. While it ran an aging Tegra X1+ processor, that was (and still is) fast for a TV media streamer. The device launched at $199.99, with a non-Pro variant at $149.99. The non-Pro Shield has since been discontinued, but the Shield TV Pro lives on at the new $299.99 price.
Nvidia has confirmed that you can blame AI for the higher Shield TV pricing. “Starting October 2, SHIELD Pro will be priced at $299. The cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry,” a spokesperson told Ars.
When we talked to Nvidia’s Andrew Bell earlier this year, he framed the Shield as a passion project , but it looks like passion projects still have to pay the bills at Nvidia. In that interview, Bell explained that Nvidia still actively manufactures the Shield and sells every unit it makes. Without a stockpile of pre-AI hardware to sell, new Shield TV units are subject to the same supply chain constraints as today’s smartphones and computers.
Nvidia isn’t a victim here, though. As a key player in AI hyperscaling, the company is more responsible than most for the sky-high cost of components. It has also become one of the most valuable firms in the world thanks to its market-leading AI accelerators and GPUs. As a consequence, we’re seeing new products launch at higher prices than their predecessors, and many end up getting more expensive during their lifetimes. Game consoles have been particularly affected, with Nintendo , Microsoft , and Sony all bumping the prices of their current-gen hardware. The PS5 Pro, for example, has gone from $699.99 at launch in 2024 to $899.99 today.
Stock of the Shield TV Pro has been slim for the last few months, probably because it became too expensive to manufacture new units with component prices rising so quickly. At $300, it will make sense for Nvidia to churn out more devices. However, this higher price will cause an already niche set-top box to be even less appealing to people who just want to stream Netflix.
Unless you need the Shield’s extensive codec support or Plex server capability, it makes more sense to get a cheaper streamer. The Shield is still out of stock on Nvidia’s store , but it’s available at the new price from Best Buy .

articles.title_orig: Your used CPU might come with someone else’s Valorant ban
articles.title_zh: Your used CPU might come with someone else’s Valorant ban
articles.content_orig:
When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn't affect our editorial independence .
With PC hardware more expensive than it’s ever been, doubly so for gamers , you might be tempted to hunt for used parts. That’s prudent and practical…but not without its risks. In addition to the usual problems of used goods with no warranty, you might just find yourself banned from your favorite online multiplayer game after you boot up with that new upgrade installed.
What? Yes, this is a real thing that happens to people. Though from what I’ve been able to see, it’s pretty darn rare. Here’s the gist: Player A, let’s call him Vincent, gets a little too heated in his games of Valorant , and decides to use a cheat program from a less-than-reputable source. He gets caught, and his Riot user account is banned. Later Vinny Valorant gets a little hard up for cash, and decides to sell his Nvidia card on eBay to Vivian, who also plays Valorant . When she installs it in her PC and logs into the game, with her non-cheating account, Vivian gets banned right away.
That’s what’s happened to a handful of players on different competitive multiplayer games, most recently chronicled in this Reddit post from a German Valorant player . The poster said that they picked up a used Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU, which worked just fine…but found themselves instantly banned from the game when they logged in. The culprit (aside from the alleged cheater) is anti-cheat systems that tag a lot more than just your account or your IP address. Modern anti-cheat software also tags hardware, down to individual hardware components.
Upon contacting support at developer Riot, the user was told that there was nothing that would be done to alleviate the situation. Not only that, but the player’s other components, including motherboard and storage, were also blacklisted in the Vanguard anti-cheat system.
Hardware identification requires fairly deep hooks into a PC’s operating system and even BIOS. For example, Heise.de reports that Vanguard only operates if you’ve got Secure Boot and a Trusted Platform Module enabled — these are some of the reasons that games like Valorant and others still aren’t available on Linux or SteamOS . Similar anti-cheat hardware checks, and the occasional false positive after secondhand hardware goes to a new owner, have been reported for years.
Exactly what checks each anti-cheat system uses aren’t generally known. But from a hardware perspective and with those deep kernel-level tools available, it’s technically possible for the software to identify individual components including:
Various other, less invasive data points can be used to “fingerprint” individual users beyond their accounts .
I reached out to Riot, Valve, and Epic Games  — operators of Vanguard, Valve Anti-Cheat, and Easy Anti-Cheat, respectively — for comment on this story. I asked if they could offer a guide on which hardware could be flagged, how buyers might avoid blacklisted parts on the secondary market, and what recourse an innocent deal-hunter might have if they find their account banned after installing a new part. None of them responded before publishing. Based on my research on the scant cases for the past few years, customer support is generally unwilling to lift bans put in place through hardware ID.
Again, it appears that this is an exceedingly rare problem. To experience it you’d need to buy a part secondhand, from a cheater, who plays the same game (or at least a game from a company using the same anti-cheat system), and who’s been flagged by that system for cheating. That is a very small center of a Venn diagram — you’re much more likely to just get a part that doesn’t work, or be the victim of a more conventional scam .
But with PC gamers experiencing very specific sticker shock on top of general economic anxiety, the used hardware market is thriving more than usual. That means the number of false positives has probably gone up recently, if not the actual percentage of them as a function of the total sales of used PC components. There’s no real way to know if a part has been flagged before you buy it if the seller doesn’t choose to share that information.
So yeah, if your buddy admits to using an aimbot, maybe think twice before picking up their secondhand parts after they win the lottery and spring for an upgrade.
Michael is a 15-year veteran of technology journalism, covering everything from Apple to ZTE. On PCWorld he's the resident keyboard nut, always using a new one for a review and building a new mechanical board or expanding his desktop "battlestation" in his off hours. Michael's previous bylines include Android Police, Digital Trends, Wired, Lifehacker, and How-To Geek, and he's covered events like CES and Mobile World Congress live. Michael lives in Pennsylvania where he's always looking forward to his next kayaking trip.

articles.title_orig: Watch 4 Songs From Goodspeed's The Snow Goose, Including Ally Bonino Singing 'The World Don't Want to Know'
articles.title_zh: Watch 4 Songs From Goodspeed's The Snow Goose, Including Ally Bonino Singing 'The World Don't Want to Know'
articles.content_orig:
Ashlyn Maddox, Eric Graise, Bonino, and more star in the world premiere musical version of Paul Gallico's 1940 novella.
October 02, 2026 By Andrew Gans, Logan Culwell-Block
Goodspeed Musicals' world premiere of The Snow Goose is currently playing the East Haddam, Connecticut, venue through October 18. Watch Ally Bonino sing "The World Don't Want to Know" from the new musical, which began performances August 28, in the video above.
Adapted from Paul Gallico 's 1940 novella, the musical was 
commissioned by the Goodspeed, and is written by Jonathan Larson Grant 
winners Scott Gilmour and McKenzie. Marshall Pailet ( Private Jones )
 is directing. The story follows a young man and woman who together 
rescue a wounded snow goose on the coast of England in the months before
 World War II, spawning a transformative friendship as the boy sets off 
to save soldiers trapped at Dunkirk.
The cast features Eric Graise ( Tracker , Step Up: High Water ) as Philip Rhayader, Ashlyn Maddox ( Parade ) as Frith, Sam Sherwood as The Bard, Charlie Webb ( Parade , The Notebook ) as Wilf, and Bonino ( Suffs ) as Harper. articles.title_orig: Fox Panel Loses It at Jaw-Droppingly Bad Sign for Trump
articles.title_zh: Fox Panel Loses It at Jaw-Droppingly Bad Sign for Trump
articles.content_orig:
The Fox Business panel was visibly shocked by a horror jobs report for President Donald Trump.
The report dropped during a live broadcast on Friday morning, with host Taylor Riggs delivering the news . “The numbers do not look good. I’m looking at 29,000 jobs added. That is well below expectations for 90,000, and our unemployment rate jumps up to 4.2 percent from 4.1 percent the previous month. A significant slowdown,” she remarked, looking taken aback.
The September report presents a headache for Trump, with the midterm elections just a month away and with Americans already souring on him over the state of his economy.
An exasperated Charles Payne sighed and said, “Well, you know, again, looking at this through two lenses, one lens is, ‘Hey, the market is like, oh boy.’ Just a couple of days ago, maybe 48 hours, 72 hours, an October rate hike was on the table.”
The panel laughed. Thomas Simons, chief U.S. economist at Jefferies, said in a note: “For the Fed, this number should be the nail in the coffin for an October hike,” CNBC reports.
“Not anymore, right?” Payne added on Friday morning’s broadcast. “The comfort that the hawks on the FOMC [Federal Open Market Committee] had been hiding behind was like, ‘Well, you know what? Labor’s OK. No problem there.’ So maybe this gives them a little bit of discomfort. That’s off the table. From a Wall Street perspective, you can see futures are moving a little bit higher. But...of course we gotta go through this and get the nuances of it all.”
Contributor E.J. Antoni, a public finance economist, tried to spin the numbers. After noting that unemployment was up by 78,000, he said, “But the fact that you have, what, over the last two months, almost a million additional Americans employed, that is great news. That is a sign that the economy, especially the labor market, is much stronger than I think a lot of folks are giving it credit for.”
Noting that private-sector jobs were up, contributor Lou Basenese also tried to lift the mood in the studio. “A lot of people make a stink about there being a lot of noise in this data, but the trends are relevant,” he said.
Riggs then hit the panel with some more concerning numbers.
“And you guys correct me if I’m wrong, but I’m seeing some maybe weakness in average earnings,” Riggs said. “Charles, I know that you were hot on this month-over-month average earnings, 0.13 percent versus the 0.3. And earnings year over year three instead of the 3.2 expectations. So sort of the earnings may be coming down?”
“Yeah,” Payne said, sounding down. “Or the rate of growth has slowed dramatically.”
“That exacerbates this inflationary situation because, you know, you go and the gasoline is up, but the rate of growth of your wages is not.”
Prosperity co-founder and former Trump economic adviser, Steve Moore, was called on to improve the mood. “Well, obviously it’s a disappointing number. I was hoping for closer to 75 to 100,000 jobs,” he declared.
U.S. stock futures climbed early Friday, signaling a higher opening on Wall Street. Futures tied to the S&P 500 rose 0.8 percent, while the Dow was set to gain 458 points, or 0.9 percent. The tech-heavy Nasdaq was up 1.2 percent.
Bond yields fell, with the yield on 10-year Treasury notes down more than five basis points to 5.176 percent.
In response to a request for comment, the White House directed the Beast to a post on X from spokesperson Taylor Rogers, who focused on private-sector growth and did not mention rising unemployment.
“More than one million private-sector jobs have now been created under President Trump. In September, the private sector added jobs, and labor participation rose, while President Trump has shrunk the federal bureaucracy to the lowest levels since the 1960s,” she said.
“The economy added 9,000 manufacturing jobs and 12,300 factory construction jobs over the month—proof that President Trump’s reindustrialization agenda is working. Wages are up over the past year, core inflation is down, and everyday Americans are reaping the rewards of the strong Trump economy.”

articles.title_orig: Fighting Intensifies in Yemen, Raising Fears Further of All-Out War
articles.title_zh: Fighting Intensifies in Yemen, Raising Fears Further of All-Out War
articles.content_orig:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels conducted intense attacks across frontlines in Taiz governorate on Thursday, as the Iran-allied group attempts to build on its lighting offensive that captured the country’s Red Sea coast last month.
Thus far, Yemeni government forces have been able to hold their positions on the frontlines and even claimed to have inflicted heavy losses against the Houthis.
Still, there are few signs that the Saudi-backed government intends to begin a serious counteroffensive against the Houthis in the near future, despite the head of Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council Rashad al-Alimi calling for a general mobilisation against the rebels on September 25.
The government instead seems to be pursuing a more gradual process, building up its military forces and attempting to make them more cohesive.
Abdul Basir al-Bahr, a senior official with the internationally recognised government army’s Taiz Military Axis, told Al Jazeera that the general mobilisation call was part of that effort.
Al-Bahr said plans include bringing reserve personnel back into the military’s ranks and retraining them, alongside local anti-Houthi fighters and civilian volunteers.
He stressed that the measures were at an early stage and their battlefield impact could not be judged yet.
In Taiz, Al Jazeera’s field monitoring has found that fighting has continued since early September without any major shifts that can be directly attributed to the general mobilisation.
The picture is similar on other fronts, including the Kahboub Mountains overlooking the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, and in Lahj, south of Taiz.
Yemeni government field commanders told Al Jazeera the general mobilisation had not yet led to frontline reinforcements.
But that does not mean that military activity has not intensified. On Monday, Colonel Majid al-Nazili, spokesman for the government’s military forces, said the forces had carried out more than 400 strikes over a 24-hour period against the Houthis, causing losses in personnel and equipment.
The ability of the Yemeni government’s military to halt further Houthi advances since the Red Sea reversal appears to reflect a combination of more favourable defensive terrain in the Taiz mountains and Lahj, as well as increased firepower.
The loss of the coastline was aided by weak coordination among anti-Houthi forces, who – despite officially being under one military chain of command – appeared divided and unable to respond quickly to the Houthi advance.
In both Taiz and Lahj – as well as Marib in Yemen’s north – anti-Houthi forces have shown more unity and have years of experience preventing Houthi military advances. Government-aligned forces have also had time to reinforce areas where the Houthis are attempting to advance.
The use of air power is also growing, with government forces reporting hundreds of air, drone, artillery and other strikes targeting Houthi positions and reinforcements in the past few days.
After having seized stretches of the Red Sea coast, the Houthis now need control of the mountainous high ground overlooking Bab al-Mandeb and the roads leading inland to consolidate those gains. Their attempts to take that high ground have so far failed, while the expanded territory has increased the manpower and logistical burden of defending their new positions.
The result, so far, is increasingly a battle over roads and supply lines, with neither side so far able to reproduce the kind of rapid breakthrough seen on the Red Sea coast.
Al Jazeera’s Yemen Editor, Ahmed al-Shalafi, said that the current Houthi attack on Taiz was the result of the group’s desire to secure its coastal gains, as well as an attempt to separate government forces.
He attributed their lack of success so far to a number of reasons.
“When you are talking about Taiz, you’re not just talking about Taiz itself, Taiz is connected to Lahj, Aden, Hodeidah, it has political importance, geographical importance, military importance,” al-Shalafi said.
“There is a difference between the Houthis entering Mocha and between them entering Taiz [city],” he added. “Firstly, the front is strong, there is a cohesion between the tribes and the local forces and the government forces … Secondly, the Houthis do not have a strong base of support in Taiz.”

articles.title_orig: Pixel 10a gets a $100 price hike, now starting at $599
articles.title_zh: Pixel 10a gets a $100 price hike, now starting at $599
articles.content_orig:
Google has quietly raised the price of its mid-range Pixel 10a by $100, giving the device a starting price of $599.
Effective as of today at the Google Store, Pixel 10a has jumped from $499 to $599. The reason is obvious, of course, with the current skyrocketing costs of components such as memory. Google has not officially commented on the price hike yet, though.
This follows Google issuing a price increas e to each of its new Pixel 11 devices compared to the prior generation.
When Google confirmed the Pixel 11 would be more expensive, the company said that this would eventually impact “in-market Pixel phones” which, at the time, we speculated could include Pixel 10a.
The 128GB base Pixel 10a is $599 as of today, with the 256GB model at $699. The updated prices have already kicked in at Amazon and Best Buy , and Google Store now shows Pixel 10a at $849 in Canada, £599 in the UK, and €649 in Europe.
However, this could be fine IF it means the 11a will come at the same $599 price and with Tensor G6 and PixelSnap magnets.
Hopefully street price for those wanting to buy a 10a soon won't change much.
In our review of Pixel 10a , we called the device a “well-rounded experience” for its $499 price, but a $100 jump certainly makes that a tougher conversation, especially considering Google’s mid-ranger is at this point using a two-generation-old chipset in its Tensor G4. But, of course, Google is far from alone here. Just this week, Samsung also issued price hikes across the Galaxy lineup including flagship and mid-range devices alike.

articles.title_orig: The Endhó Dam: One of the World’s Least Known Sacrifice Zones
articles.title_zh: The Endhó Dam: One of the World’s Least Known Sacrifice Zones
articles.content_orig:
Environmental Law and Climate Policy Insights
Last week, about halfway down the New York Times’ Monday morning newsletter, there was a video titled “ Living Next to Mexico’s Toxic Reservoir .”  I watched it, appalled not only by the dangerous conditions described in the video and accompanying article , but also by the fact that I had never heard of this enormous environmental justice disaster.  I worried that if I—someone who inevitably spends some part of everyday thinking about environmental injustices—was previously unaware that over 20,000 people have been forced to live around a toxic reservoir for approximately five decades , then it was unlikely that these communities had been receiving much, if any, attention and support from environmental organizations outside of the region.  It turns out that, unfortunately, my concern was well-founded.  In 2023, Judges for the Society of Environmental Journalists’ 22nd Annual Awards for Reporting on the Environment awarded “ Los Olvidados de Hidalgo ” [English transcript here ]—a N+ Focus feature story about the Endhó Dam—third place, in part because of how “shockingly unknown” the story was.
The Endhó Dam was built in the 1950s as a freshwater reservoir, and for about 20 years, it served as such.  There was plenty of clean water to irrigate the crops in the otherwise arid Mezquital Valley, and the dam provided locals with an enjoyable and clean natural environment .  In the 1970s, however, as the population of Mexico City continued to grow, federal officials decided to begin diverting the capital’s storm runoff and wastewater into the dam.  This means that for the past 50 years, all of the wastewater from a metropolitan area of around 20 million people has been dumped into the Endhó Dam.  Every year, the dam receives around 326 million cubic meters of largely untreated wastewater—that’s enough wastewater to fill over 130,000 Olympic-sized swimming pools. Approximately 60% of the wastewater does pass through a treatment plant, but before the treated water can make it to the reservoir, it mixes with discharge and waste from a nearby oil refinery, thermopower plant, and the rest of the massive industrial corridor that surrounds the dam.  The result is an environmental and public health nightmare, referred to by locals as “ Mexico’s toilet bowl ,” and “the world’s largest cesspool.”
Yury Uribe, a lifelong resident of the region and activist with El Movimiento Social por la Tierra, has been organizing her community in an attempt to get the Mexican government to recognize the Endhó Dam as an environmental emergency, but through no fault of her own, she has seen little success.  Although the area was declared an ecological restoration zone in 2024, the declaration did not allocate any funding to cleaning up the area.  Accordingly, Endhó Dam residents continue to suffer from seemingly endless environmental and health problems.  Cancer rates in the area tripled between 2007­–2018, and today,
communities surrounding the dam report rates of cancer and kidney failures that are sometimes double the national average ; the dam contaminates the surrounding towns’ wells —the main source of drinking water for those towns’ residents; and the hyacinth that grows on top of the dam has become a breeding ground for mosquitos , endangering locals’ livestock and forcing residents to “ lock themselves inside ” every evening.  Emiliano Rodríguez Mega, a long-time science reporter covering Latin America and the NYT reporter who covered this story, said that even he “ had never quite seen something like the Endhó Dam .”
The big question that normally follows learning about an injustice like this is, “how is this allowed to happen?”  Unfortunately, the answer this time is the same as it almost always is:  some communities—low-income, marginalized communities—are seen as expendable.  As explained by the legendary environmental justice advocates Dr. Robert Bullard and Beverly Wright, the people and communities who are viewed as being expendable suffer from having “ the wrong complexion for protection .”
Areas like the Endhó Dam are often referred to as “ sacrifice zones ” because “the health and safety of people in these communities is being effectively sacrificed for the economic gains and prosperity of others.”  In this instance, the low-income farming communities living around the dam ( a substantial percentage of whom are Indigenous , primarily from the Otomí Nation ) are being sacrificed to protect Mexico City from flooding and to keep the profitable agricultural area surrounding the Tula River rich with nutrients.  Similar cases of environmental injustice and racism exist around the world:  the risk of cancer to the primarily Black residents of “Cancer Alley” in Louisiana is over 50 times higher than the national average; 95% of children in Kabwe, Zambia , largely from poor families, have dangerously elevated levels of lead in their blood caused by the nearby lead mining; nearly every Aamjiwnaang First Nation household living in Canada’s “Chemical Valley” suffers from high rates of miscarriages, asthma, and cancer.  The examples, unfortunately, abound.  Recognizing that these areas “illustrat[e] egregious human rights violations, particularly of poor, vulnerable and marginalized communities,” former United Nations Special Rapporteur on Human Rights and the Environment, David Boyd, described sacrifice zones as “ the worst imaginable dereliction of a State’s obligation to respect, protect, and fulfil[l] the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment.”
How do we finally rid the world of a system in which, as Naomi Klein put it in This Changes Everything , “poisoning [whole subsets of humanity] in the name of progress [is] somehow acceptable”?  Like most things worth doing, it’s somewhat complicated.  But as the Climate Justice Alliance—an alliance of over 100 frontline communities in the climate justice movement— has noted , it is critically necessary not only because everyone has a right to drink clean water and breathe clean air, but also because “[o]ur society cannot build a more just and healthy economy if communities continue to be seen as expendable.”  Eliminating sacrifice zones can be distilled into a three-stage process:  (1) prioritize protecting the communities living in sacrifice zones from further harm; (2) allocate resources to repairing the harm that has already been done and passing strong regulations; and (3) invest in the communities that have historically been viewed as expendable, and ensure that they have power over their own futures.  Let’s get to work.
